the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾: إن and its noun. ﴿لَعَلى هُدىً﴾: attached to the omitted khabar, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾: naʿt of هدى; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive and إن is a jussive-governing conditional. ﴿جادَلُوكَ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw of the plural; the wāw is the fāʿil; it is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَقُلِ﴾: the fāʾ binds the apodosis; an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. ﴿اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ﴾: the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ and أعلم is its khabar; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بِما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and ما is relative; both attached to أعلم. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is ṣila (relative clause). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَحْكُمُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is khabar, and the clause الله يحكم is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾: an adverb of place attached to يحكم, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِيما﴾: في is a preposition and ما is relative; both attached to يحكم. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: كان and its noun; the clause is ṣila. ﴿فِيهِ﴾: attached to تختلفون. ﴿تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم.

daas-irab:70-71.t: ﴿أَلَمْ﴾: the hamza is for the interrogation of affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī), and لم is a particle of negation, jussive and conversion (to the past). ﴿تَعْلَمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: أن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; [this is] to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in place of the two objects of تعلم. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن. ﴿ما﴾: relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِي السَّماءِ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to السماء. ﴿أَنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: ذا is a demonstrative in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the noun of إن; the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. [Translator's note: the Quranic text is ﴿إِنَّ ذلِكَ فِي كِتابٍ﴾; the source's heading has أنّ while its analysis says إن.] ﴿فِي كِتابٍ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿إِنَّ ذلِكَ﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾: attached to يسير. ﴿يَسِيرٌ﴾: the khabar of إن; the two clauses are causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾: attached to يعبدون. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ما﴾: relative, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَمْ﴾: a particle of negation, conversion and jussive. ﴿يُنَزِّلْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive; the clause is ṣila. ﴿بِهِ﴾: attached to ينزل. ﴿سُلْطاناً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾: relative, conjoined to the preceding ما. ﴿لَيْسَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: the lām is a preposition and the hāʾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr); both attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿بِهِ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿عِلْمٌ﴾: the postponed noun of ليس; the clause of ليس is the ṣila of ما. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a particle of resumption and ما is negative. ﴿لِلظَّالِمِينَ﴾: attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿نَصِيرٍ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, whose appearance is prevented by the place being occupied with the vowel of the redundant preposition. The clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:72-72.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb containing the meaning of condition. ﴿تُتْلى﴾: a passive imperfect verb; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) تتلى. ﴿آياتُنا﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from آياتنا, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿تَعْرِفُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿فِي وُجُوهِ﴾: attached to تعرف. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is ṣila (relative clause). ﴿الْمُنْكَرَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَكادُونَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its noun; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿يَسْطُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of يكادون. ﴿بِالَّذِينَ﴾: الذين is a relative noun; both attached to يسطون. ﴿يَتْلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is ṣila. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: attached to يتلون. ﴿آياتُنا﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَفَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle; an imperfect verb and a mafʿūl bihi, the mīm for the plural, and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بِشَرٍّ﴾: attached to أنبئكم. ﴿مِنْ ذلِكُمُ﴾: attached to شر; ذا is a demonstrative, the lām is for distance, the kāf for address and the mīm for the plural. ﴿النَّارُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَعَدَهَا﴾: a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, a postponed fāʿil; the clause is khabar. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is ṣila. ﴿وَبِئْسَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and بئس is a past verb for expressing blame. ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾: fāʿil; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:73-74.t: ﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle. ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾: the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied أدعو (I call); the hāʾ is a particle of alerting (tanbīh) with no grammatical position. ﴿النَّاسُ﴾: badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the clause is resumptive. ﴿ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ﴾: a passive past verb and nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿فَاسْتَمِعُوا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لَهُ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) استمعوا; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: relative, in the position of accusative as the noun of إن; the clause إن الذين is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿تَدْعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَنْ يَخْلُقُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative by لن, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn. ﴿ذُباباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إن. ﴿وَلَوِ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿اجْتَمَعُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُ﴾: attached to اجتمعوا; the clause is conjoined; the clause اجتمعوا is the clause of the condition, initial, with no grammatical position; and the apodosis of لو is omitted, its implied form being "لا يقدرون" (they would not be able). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive and إن is conditional. ﴿يَسْلُبْهُمُ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الذُّبابُ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is initial, with no grammatical position. ﴿لا يَسْتَنْقِذُوهُ﴾: لا is negative; an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾: attached to the verb before it; the clause has no grammatical position because it is not joined to the binding fāʾ. ﴿ضَعُفَ الطَّالِبُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَالْمَطْلُوبُ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الطالب; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾: negative. ﴿قَدَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾: the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿حَقَّ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿قَدْرِهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ﴾: إن, its noun and its two khabars, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:75-77.t: ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَصْطَفِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) because of heaviness; the clause is khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) يصطفي or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause الله يصطفي is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿رُسُلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to من الملائكة. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ﴾: إن, its noun and its two khabars; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾: relative, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾: an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَما﴾: relative, conjoined to the preceding ما. ﴿خَلْفَهُمْ﴾: an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَإِلَى اللَّهِ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to ترجع. ﴿تُرْجَعُ﴾: a passive imperfect verb. ﴿الْأُمُورُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined. ﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle. ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾: the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), in the position of accusative (manṣūb) by the vocative; the hāʾ is for alerting (tanbīh). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is ṣila. ﴿ارْكَعُوا﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَاسْجُدُوا﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَاعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَافْعَلُوا الْخَيْرَ﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾: لعل and its noun, and the mīm is for the plural. ﴿تُفْلِحُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لعل.

daas-irab:78-78.t: ﴿وَجاهِدُوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined. [Translator's note: جاهدوا here is an imperative verb; the source says "past".] ﴿فِي اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty is genitive (majrūr) by في; both attached to (mutaʿalliq) جاهدوا. ﴿حَقَّ﴾: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, standing in for the absolute object). ﴿جِهادِهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿هُوَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿اجْتَباكُمْ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif because of impossibility; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the mīm is for the plural, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is khabar (predicate). ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿جَعَلَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: attached to جعل; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِي الدِّينِ﴾: attached to جعل. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿حَرَجٍ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) in position and genitive in wording by the vowel of the redundant preposition. ﴿مِلَّةَ﴾: accusative by specialisation (ikhtiṣāṣ), i.e. "أخص ملة" (I mean specifically the creed). ﴿أَبِيكُمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the yāʾ because it is one of the five nouns, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the fatḥa because it is a diptote, owing to being a proper name and foreign. [Translator's note: إبراهيم is more commonly parsed as badal (substitute) of أبيكم; the source says muḍāf ilayhi.] ﴿هُوَ﴾: mubtadaʾ; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿سَمَّاكُمُ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif because of impossibility; the kāf is first mafʿūl bihi and the mīm is for the plural; the clause is khabar. ﴿الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾: attached to سماكم; قبل is indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning. ﴿وَفِي هذا﴾: ذا is a demonstrative in the position of genitive by the preposition; both attached to an omitted verb indicated by what precedes, and it is conjoined to من قبل. ﴿لِيَكُونَ﴾: the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and يكون is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb. ﴿الرَّسُولُ﴾: the noun of كان. ﴿شَهِيداً﴾: khabar. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: attached to شهيدا; [the implied] أن, the lām and what follows them are to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), both attached to سماكم. ﴿وَتَكُونُوا﴾: an incomplete imperfect verb conjoined to what precedes it, accusative by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its noun. ﴿شُهَداءَ﴾: khabar. ﴿عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾: attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective). ﴿فَأَقِيمُوا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الصَّلاةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَآتُوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and آتوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الزَّكاةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَاعْتَصِمُوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: attached to اعتصموا. ﴿هُوَ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَوْلاكُمْ﴾: khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied on the alif because of impossibility; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi and the mīm is for the plural; the clause is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَنِعْمَ الْمَوْلى﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; نعم is a past verb for expressing praise, and المولى is its fāʿil, nominative with the ḍamma implied on the alif because of impossibility; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ﴾: a past verb that comes for expressing praise, and النصير is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes, and like it has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:1-2.t: ﴿يا﴾ for the vocative. ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite noun (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied (muqaddar) أدعو; and ها is for calling attention (tanbīh). ﴿النَّاسُ﴾ badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the vocative clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿اتَّقُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَبَّكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause has no grammatical position because it is initial. ﴿إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ شَيْءٌ﴾ إن, its noun and its khabar (predicate), and الساعة is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of شيء; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) تذهل. ﴿تَرَوْنَها﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and ها is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مُرْضِعَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ عن is a preposition and ما is relative; the two are attached to تذهل. ﴿أَرْضَعَتْ﴾ a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause is ordinarily the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.] ﴿وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to تذهل. ﴿ذاتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿حَمْلٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿حَمْلَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and ها is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَتَرَى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur), its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿النَّاسَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿سُكارى﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb); the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and ما is negating, operating like ليس. ﴿هُمْ﴾ the noun of ما, in the position of the nominative. ﴿بِسُكارى﴾ the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and سكارى is the khabar, genitive in form, accusative in position; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ﴾ لكن, its noun and its khabar, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to the ḥāl clause and, like it, is in the position of the accusative.

daas-irab:3-7.t: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the nominative as postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. [Translator's note: the parsed word is the relative noun ﴿مَنْ﴾ of the verse; the source vocalises it مِنَ, here and below.] ﴿يُجادِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿فِي اللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to يجادل. ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being جاهلا. ﴿عِلْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَيَتَّبِعُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿شَيْطانٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مَرِيدٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective). ﴿كُتِبَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to كتب. ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ أن and its noun, [forming] an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of كتب. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, or a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿تَوَلَّاهُ﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur), its fāʿil latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَأَنَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis, and أن and its noun; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿يُضِلُّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar of أن. ﴿وَيَهْدِيهِ﴾ the clause is conjoined to يضله. ﴿إِلى عَذابِ﴾ the two are attached to يهديه. ﴿السَّعِيرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its apodosis is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من. ﴿يا﴾ for the vocative. ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite noun (nakira maqṣūda), in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of an implied أدعو; and ها is for calling attention (tanbīh). ﴿النَّاسُ﴾ badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). ﴿إِنْ﴾ a jussive-governing conditional particle. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿فِي رَيْبٍ﴾ the two are attached to the khabar of كان. ﴿مِنَ الْبَعْثِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of ريب. ﴿فَإِنَّا﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis; إن, and نا is its noun. ﴿خَلَقْناكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the khabar of إن, and the [whole] clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿مِنْ تُرابٍ﴾ the two are attached to خلقناكم. ﴿ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ مُضْغَةٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿مُخَلَّقَةٍ﴾ a naʿt of مضغة. ﴿وَغَيْرِ﴾ conjoined to مخلقة. ﴿مُخَلَّقَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām of causation (taʿlīl), its fāʿil latent; أن and what follows it are an interpreted maṣdar, [and with the lām] the two are attached to خلقناكم. ﴿وَنُقِرُّ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿فِي الْأَرْحامِ﴾ the two are attached to نقر; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿نَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِلى أَجَلٍ﴾ the two are attached to نقر. ﴿مُسَمًّى﴾ a naʿt of أجل. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿نُخْرِجُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿طِفْلًا﴾ a ḥāl or a tamyīz (specification). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لِتَبْلُغُوا﴾ the lām is for causation, and the imperfect verb is accusative by the implied أن after it, [its accusative marked] by deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the lām and what follows it, as an interpreted maṣdar, are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being نعمركم. ﴿أَشُدَّكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَمِنْكُمْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the two are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنَ﴾ relative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُتَوَفَّى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرَدُّ﴾ see the parsing of what precedes it. ﴿إِلى أَرْذَلِ﴾ the two are attached to يرد. ﴿الْعُمُرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِكَيْلا﴾ the lām is a preposition, كي is an accusative-governing particle, and لا is negating. ﴿يَعْلَمَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by كي, and its fāʿil is latent; the imperfect verb, as an interpreted maṣdar, is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the two are attached to يرد. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ the two are attached to يعلم. ﴿عِلْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied ḍamma, its fāʿil latent, and الأرض is its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿هامِدَةً﴾ ḥāl, accusative. ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb for future time. ﴿أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهَا الْماءَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object, and عليها: the two are attached to أنزلنا; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اهْتَزَّتْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَرَبَتْ﴾ conjoined to اهتزت, like it. ﴿وَأَنْبَتَتْ﴾ the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ the two are attached to أنبتت. ﴿زَوْجٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَهِيجٍ﴾ a naʿt, genitive (majrūr). ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ أن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; its clause, interpreted as a maṣdar, is in the position of the genitive, [and with the bāʾ] the two are attached to an omitted [khabar], its implied form being شاهد. ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أن. ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and أن and its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يُحْيِ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْمَوْتى﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative with an implied fatḥa on the alif owing to impossibility; the clause is the khabar of أن. ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ its parsing is like the preceding one, and the clause is likewise conjoined to what precedes. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ the two are attached to قدير. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of أن, nominative. ﴿وَأَنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; أن, its noun and its khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لا رَيْبَ﴾ لا is the lā of generic negation, and ريب is its noun. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the khabar; the clause is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in آتية. ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; أن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَبْعَثُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent; the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أن. ﴿مَنْ﴾ relative, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي الْقُبُورِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila.

daas-irab:8-10.t: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the nominative as postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. [Translator's note: the parsed word is the relative noun ﴿مَنْ﴾ of the verse; the source vocalises it مِنَ.] ﴿يُجادِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿فِي اللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to يجادل. ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عِلْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلا هُدىً وَلا كِتابٍ﴾ conjoined by the conjunctions. ﴿مُنِيرٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب, genitive (majrūr) like it. ﴿ثانِيَ﴾ ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb). ﴿عِطْفِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِيُضِلَّ﴾ the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and يضل is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām of causation; its fāʿil is هو; the clause, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), is in the position of the genitive, and the two are attached to يجادل. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾ the two are attached to يضل. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا﴾ الدنيا is a genitive noun, genitive with an implied (muqaddar) kasra on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the two are attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿خِزْيٌ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَنُذِيقُهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to نذيقه. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْحَرِيقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿بِما﴾ ما is relative, and the two are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿قَدَّمَتْ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿يَداكَ﴾ fāʿil, nominative with the alif because it is a dual, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ذلك is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech) of an omitted verb. ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ أن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَيْسَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun omitted. ﴿بِظَلَّامٍ﴾ the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and ظلام is the khabar of ليس, genitive in form, accusative in position; the clause of ليس with its noun and khabar is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أن. ﴿لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾ the two are attached to ظلام.

daas-irab:11-13.t: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنَ﴾ relative, in the position of the nominative as postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. [Translator's note: the parsed word is the relative noun ﴿مَنْ﴾ of the verse; the source vocalises it مِنَ.] ﴿يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and its object is the Name of Majesty, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿عَلى حَرْفٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of يعبد. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive and إن is conditional. ﴿أَصابَهُ خَيْرٌ﴾ a past verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil. ﴿اطْمَأَنَّ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition not joined to the fāʾ or to the إذا of surprise. به: the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and إن is conditional. ﴿أَصابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ﴾ a past verb, its object and its postponed fāʿil, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first إن etc. ﴿انْقَلَبَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿عَلى وَجْهِهِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a condition not joined to the fāʾ or to the إذا of surprise. ﴿خَسِرَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur). ﴿وَالْآخِرَةَ﴾ conjoined to الدنيا, like it; the clause is resumptive or a ḥāl from the fāʿil of انقلب. ﴿وذلك﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a second mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْخُسْرانُ﴾ khabar of the second mubtadaʾ, and the clause هو الخسران is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْمُبِينُ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of الخسران, nominative (marfūʿ) like it. ﴿يَدْعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the wāw owing to heaviness, its fāʿil latent. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾ relative, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا يَضُرُّهُ﴾ لا is negating; an imperfect verb and its object, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَما لا يَنْفَعُهُ﴾ its parsing is like the preceding one, and it is conjoined. ﴿ذلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلالُ الْبَعِيدُ﴾ its parsing is like ذلك هو الخسران المبين. ﴿يَدْعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the wāw owing to heaviness, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَمَنْ﴾ the lām is for commencement (ibtidāʾ) or paves the way for an oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam). ﴿مِنْ﴾ a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿ضَرُّهُ﴾ a second mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَقْرَبُ﴾ khabar of ضره; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْ نَفْعِهِ﴾ the two are attached to أقرب. ﴿لَبِئْسَ﴾ the lām is the lām of commencement or occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame. ﴿الْمَوْلى﴾ fāʿil of بئس, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility; the clause is the khabar of من. ﴿وَلَبِئْسَ الْعَشِيرُ﴾ its parsing is like the preceding one.

daas-irab:14-15.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ إن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُدْخِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is joined to the wāw of the group, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the kasra. ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness; الأنهار is its fāʿil, and من تحتها: the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تجري; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of جنات, in the position of the accusative. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ إن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَفْعَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar of إن. ﴿ما﴾ relative, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يُرِيدُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is a ṣila with no grammatical position. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a jussive-governing conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun omitted, its implied form being هو. ﴿يَظُنُّ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar of كان. ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy أنّ, its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لَنْ﴾ an accusative-governing particle. ﴿يَنْصُرَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative, and its fronted object, and the Name of Majesty is its postponed fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of أن, and أن and what follows it, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), fill the place of the two objects of يظن. ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا﴾ the two are attached to ينصره. ﴿وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ conjoined to الدنيا, genitive (majrūr) like it. ﴿فَلْيَمْدُدْ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, the lām is the lām of command, and the imperfect verb is jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause of condition and apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of من. ﴿بِسَبَبٍ﴾ that is, the rope; and السماء here is the ceiling — i.e. whoever despairs of the mercy of Allah, let him hang himself and see whether that brings him any benefit; the two are attached to يمدد. ﴿إِلَى السَّماءِ﴾ the two are attached to يمدد. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لْيَقْطَعْ﴾ its parsing is like ليمدد, and the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرْ﴾ its parsing is like the preceding one. ﴿هَلْ﴾ an interrogative particle. ﴿يُذْهِبَنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis. ﴿كَيْدُهُ﴾ fāʿil, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ما﴾ relative, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the mafʿūl bihi of ينظر. ﴿يَغِيظُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is a ṣila with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-17.t: ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the kāf is for comparison and ذا is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive by the kāf; the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). ﴿أَنْزَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿آياتٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾ a naʿt, genitive (majrūr) like the noun it qualifies. [Translator's note: so in the source; as a naʿt of the accusative آيات it is accusative, with the kasra.] ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ أن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; its clause is conjoined to the hāʾ in أنزلناه. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن. ﴿يُرِيدُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, the noun of إن. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to the الذين before it. ﴿هادُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes, and its parsing is like it. ﴿وَالصَّابِئِينَ﴾ they are the worshippers of the stars; conjoined to the noun of إن, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿وَالنَّصارى﴾ conjoined to الذين; it is accusative like it, with an implied fatḥa on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur). ﴿وَالْمَجُوسَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun whose position is the accusative, like what it is conjoined to. ﴿أَشْرَكُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ إن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿يَفْصِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place attached to يفصل, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to يفصل. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause إن الله etc. is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the first إن. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is the noun of إن. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to the khabar. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَهِيدٌ﴾ the khabar of إن, nominative; the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿أَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and لم is a particle of negation, jussive government and conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning]. ﴿تَرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by deletion of the weak letter, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنت; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is the noun of أن, and أن and what follows it fill the place of the two objects of تر. ﴿يَسْجُدُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يسجد. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of يسجد. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ وَالنُّجُومُ وَالْجِبالُ وَالشَّجَرُ وَالدَّوَابُّ وَكَثِيرٌ﴾ conjoined to the first من. ﴿مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ the two are attached to كثير. ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and كثير is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حَقَّ﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to حق. ﴿الْعَذابُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كثير, and the clause of the mubtadaʾ and its khabar is resumptive. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُهِنِ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by من; it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and it is given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. [Translator's note: the source heads it with a fatḥa (اللَّهَ); as fāʿil it is ﴿اللَّهُ﴾, as in the verse.] ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, and ما is negating. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. [Translator's note: the verse reads ﴿مِنْ﴾; the source writes مَنْ.] ﴿مُكْرِمٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form, nominative in position as the postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is joined to the fāʾ. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is the noun of إن, accusative (manṣūb); the clause is resumptive. [Translator's note: the verse reads ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾, as the source's analysis assumes.] ﴿يَفْعَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being هو. ﴿ما﴾ relative, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of إن. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:19-21.t: ﴿هذانِ﴾ the hā is for calling attention (tanbīh), and ذان is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). [Translator's note: so in the source; ذان is more commonly described as nominative with the alif, as a dual.] ﴿خَصْمانِ﴾ khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with the alif because it is a dual; the clause is resumptive. ﴿اخْتَصَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of خصمان. ﴿فِي رَبِّهِمْ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) اختصموا, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَالَّذِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and الذين is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيابٌ﴾ a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; ثياب is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and لهم: the two are attached to قطعت; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ نارٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of ثياب. ﴿يُصَبُّ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْ فَوْقِ﴾ the two are attached to يصب. ﴿رُؤُسِهِمُ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْحَمِيمُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is resumptive or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in لهم. ﴿يُصْهَرُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to يصهر. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿فِي بُطُونِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْجُلُودُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; الجلود is conjoined to ما and is nominative like it. ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and لهم: the two are attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿مَقامِعُ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ حَدِيدٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of مقامع.

daas-irab:22-24.t: ﴿كُلَّما﴾ an adverb containing the meaning of condition. ﴿أَرادُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿أَنْ﴾ accusative-governing. ﴿يَخْرُجُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the sign of its accusative being the deletion of the nūn; the clause, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أرادوا. ﴿مِنْها﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يخرجوا. ﴿مِنْ غَمٍّ﴾ the two are attached to يخرجوا. ﴿أُعِيدُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of كلما. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to أعيدوا. ﴿وَذُوقُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ذوقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the omitted verb قيل. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْحَرِيقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ إن, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿يُدْخِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being هو; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إن. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ conjoined to it, and its parsing is like it. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness. ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ the two are attached to تجري. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات. ﴿يُحَلَّوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ أَساوِرَ﴾ من is redundant (zāʾida), and أساور is mafʿūl bihi, genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa because it is a diptote, accusative in position. ﴿مِنْ ذَهَبٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of أساور. ﴿وَلُؤْلُؤاً﴾ conjoined to the position of من أساور, or the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being ويؤتون. ﴿وَلِباسُهُمْ فِيها حَرِيرٌ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the clause is resumptive, and فيها: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهُدُوا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and هدوا is a passive past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is joined to the wāw of the group; the wāw is an attached pronoun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَى الطَّيِّبِ﴾ the two are attached to هدوا. ﴿مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from الطيب. ﴿وَهُدُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and هدوا is a passive past verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿إِلى صِراطِ﴾ the two are attached to هدوا. ﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preceding one.

daas-irab:25-26.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the noun of إن; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is joined to the wāw of the group, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيَصُدُّونَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to كفروا. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يصدون. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْمَسْجِدِ﴾ conjoined to سبيل. ﴿الْحَرامِ﴾ a naʿt (adjective). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of, or badal (substitute) from, المسجد. ﴿جَعَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿سَواءً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a ḥāl if the verb is taken as not transitive to two objects. ﴿الْعاكِفُ﴾ fāʿil of سواء. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to العاكف. ﴿وَالْبادِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and الباد is conjoined to العاكف. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُرِدْ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to يرد. ﴿بِإِلْحادٍ﴾ the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and إلحاد is genitive in form, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِظُلْمٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of إلحاد. ﴿نُذِقْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its fāʿil latent, its implied form being نحن, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the two clauses of condition and apodosis are in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of من. ﴿مِنْ عَذابٍ﴾ the two are attached to نذقه. ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ a naʿt of عذاب, genitive (majrūr) like it. ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and إذ is an adverb of time attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر. ﴿بَوَّأْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لِإِبْراهِيمَ﴾ the two are attached to بوأنا. ﴿مَكانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْبَيْتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ألا﴾ أن assimilated into لا; it is explicative (tafsīriyya). ﴿لا﴾ prohibitive. ﴿تُشْرِكْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being أنت. ﴿بِي﴾ the two are attached to تشرك. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative. ﴿وَطَهِّرْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being أنت; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بَيْتِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker, its appearance prevented by the place being occupied by the suitable vowel, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِلطَّائِفِينَ﴾ the two are attached to طهر. ﴿وَالْقائِمِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and القائمين is a conjoined noun, genitive like it with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿وَالرُّكَّعِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿السُّجُودِ﴾ a naʿt, genitive with the kasra.

daas-irab:27-29.t: ﴿وَأَذِّنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; أذن is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنت; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes. ﴿فِي النَّاسِ﴾ ﴿بِالْحَجِّ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أذن. ﴿يَأْتُوكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by deletion of the nūn because it is the response to the command (jawāb al-ṭalab); the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the response to the command. ﴿رِجالًا﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is "on foot". ﴿وَعَلى كُلِّ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to an omitted ḥāl, its implied form being وركبانا على كل, and it is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ضامِرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَأْتِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ضامر. [Translator's note: so in the source; in يأتين the nūn is that of the feminine plural and is itself the fāʿil, the verb being indeclinable on the sukūn.] ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ the two are attached to يأتين. ﴿فَجٍّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; it means "road". ﴿عَمِيقٍ﴾ a naʿt; together they mean "distant". ﴿لِيَشْهَدُوا﴾ the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and the imperfect verb is accusative (manṣūb) by the implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām of causation, [marked] by deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive, [and with the lām] the two are attached to أذن. ﴿مَنافِعَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to منافع. ﴿وَيَذْكُرُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined to يشهدوا, and its parsing is like it. ﴿اسْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِي أَيَّامٍ﴾ the two are attached to يذكروا. ﴿معدودات﴾ a naʿt of أيام, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra. ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ relative; the two are attached to يذكروا. ﴿رَزَقَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent, and the hāʾ is its object and the mīm is for the group; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ بَهِيمَةِ﴾ the two are attached to رزقهم. ﴿الْأَنْعامِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَكُلُوا﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it occurs as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿مِنْها﴾ the two are attached to كلوا. ﴿وَأَطْعِمُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined, and its parsing is like it. ﴿الْبائِسَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْفَقِيرَ﴾ a naʿt, accusative. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لْيَقْضُوا﴾ the lām is the lām of command, and the imperfect verb is jussive by the lām of command, [marked] by deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿تَفَثَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلْيُوفُوا﴾ its parsing is like ليقضوا, and it is conjoined to it. ﴿نُذُورَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا﴾ like وليوفوا, conjoined. ﴿بِالْبَيْتِ﴾ the two are attached to يطوفوا. ﴿الْعَتِيقِ﴾ a naʿt.

dervis-irab:5-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النطفة): the fluid of the man or the woman; the plural is نطاف and نطف. It is what is known as المني (semen), on the pattern of فني, and المنيّ on the pattern of إليّ, and المنية on the pattern of رمية; it is pluralised as منى on the pattern of قفل.
منى, أمنى and منّى have one and the same meaning. النطفة is also clear water, whether little or much. More will be said about it later.
(عَلَقَةٍ): العلقة is congealed blood, which is what is meant here; also that which clings to the hand, anything that is hung up, the tree foliage on which livestock subsist, and a small black creature that sucks blood (the leech); the plural is علق.
(مُضْغَةٍ): a lump of flesh the size of what is chewed.
(مُخَلَّقَةٍ): المخلّقة is that which is fashioned evenly, smooth, free of deficiency and defect. One says خلّق السواك والعود (he shaped the tooth-stick and the rod) when he made it even and smoothed it, from their expression صخرة خلقاء (a smooth rock). It is as though Allah the Exalted creates the lumps of flesh differing and varied: some of them are complete in form and smooth of defects, and some of them are the opposite of that; and according to that variation the created beings vary in their forms and makeup.
(طِفْلًا): الطفل with a kasra on the ṭāʾ is applied to the child from the time of separation (birth) until the time of puberty. As for الطَّفل with a fatḥa, it means soft and delicate, and a woman is طفلة. As for الطَّفَل with a fatḥa on the ṭāʾ and the fāʾ, it is the time after the afternoon (ʿaṣr), from their expression طفلت الشمس when the sun inclines to setting. أطفلت المرأة means the woman came to have a child. In al-Mukhtār: الطفل is used as singular and plural; in the hadith, he ﷺ was asked about أطفال المشركين (the children of the polytheists). In al-Asās and al-Lisān, the gist of what is said is: he is a طفل, clearly in childhood (بيّن الطفولة); he did that in his childhood (طفولته); a woman and a doe are مطفل (having young); and طفّلت ولدها: she reared her child. Al-Akhṭal said, describing clouds:
إذا زعزعته الريح جرّ ذيولها ... كما زحفت عوذ ثقال تطفّل
(When the wind shakes it, it drags its trains, as heavy she-camels with newborn young creep along, tending their little ones.)
And a woman is طفلة, and طفلة الأنامل: soft (of fingertips); and بنان طفل: soft fingertips. Dhū al-Rumma said:
أسيلة مستنّ الوشاحين قانىء ... بأطرافها الحناء في سبط طفل
(Smooth where the two sashes run, the henna deep red on her fingertips, on soft, slender fingers.)
And طفل (it became soft), طفولة and طفالة. And "I will come to him في طفل الغداة and طفل العشي", that is, shortly after sunrise and shortly before sunset. The poet said:
باكرتها طفل الغداة بغارة ... والمبتغون خطار ذاك قليل
(I came upon them early, at the first light of morning, with a raid, and those who seek such a risk are few.)
And Labīd said:
فتدليت عليه قافلا ... وعلى الأرض غيابات الطّفل
(So I descended upon it on my way back, while the shadows of dusk lay upon the earth.)
And طفّلت الشمس when it drew near to setting; طفّل الليل: the night approached and cast its shadow; طفّل علينا and تطفّل (he came uninvited), and he is a طفيلي (a sponger). You say: "He kept sponging on people until he eclipsed Ṭufayl al-Aʿrās" — he was a man from Kufa to whom sponging (التطفيل) was attributed.
(أشده): it was discussed earlier, and we say here: الأشد is the perfection of strength [Translator's note: the printed text reads القول ("speech"); القوة ("strength") seems intended], intellect and discernment. It is one of the plural words for which no singular is used, and it is between thirty and forty.
(هامِدَةً): الهمود is stillness and subsidence; همدت الأرض: the earth dried up and became effaced; همد الثوب: the garment wore out.
(اهْتَزَّتْ): it moved; it is used here figuratively for the earth's bringing forth its plants by means of the water.
(رَبَتْ): it increased and rose, from ربا يربو.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِنَ الْبَعْثِ فَإِنَّا خَلَقْناكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ): the i'rab of يا أيها الناس has preceded. إن is conditional; كنتم is a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its noun; في ريب is its khabar (predicate); من البعث is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ريب. فإنا: the fāʾ links (the apodosis), and إنّ with its noun; the clause خلقناكم is its khabar; من تراب is attached to خلقناكم. His saying فإنا خلقناكم was permitted to occur as an apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) only by interpreting it as: "then what removes your doubt is that you look at the beginning of your creation."
(ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ مُضْغَةٍ مُخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ): it is conjoined with ثم to indicate an interval of time in the development of creation and its gradual progression from state to state. His saying مخلقة is a naʿt of مضغة, and غير مخلقة is conjoined to مخلقة. What is meant is a detailed account of the state of the lump of flesh: that at first it is a piece in which none of the limbs is visible, then after that they appear little by little.
(لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِي الْأَرْحامِ ما نَشاءُ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى): لنبين: the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and نبين is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the lām of causation; the lām with what follows it is attached to خلقناكم. Or the lām is for outcome and consequence (al-ṣayrūra wa-l-ʿāqiba), that is: through these acts of His there becomes clear, of His power and knowledge, what cannot be fathomed or encompassed; that is why the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of نبين was omitted. That is in order to argue from this power that whoever is able to begin creation is able to repeat it, so there is no room for denial and no ground for doubt. ونقر: the wāw is resumptive, and نقر is a nominative imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "we"; في الأرحام is attached to نقر; ما is a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause نشاء is its ṣila (relative clause); إلى أجل مسمى is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). It was made a new sentence only because the meaning is not "We created you in order to settle." مسمى is a naʿt of أجل حرف [Translator's note: the word حرف appears thus in the printed text and seems out of place], that is, (a term) whose time of emergence is extended.
(ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوا أَشُدَّكُمْ): ثم is a conjunction with interval also; نخرجكم is conjoined to نقر; the agent of نخرجكم is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we", and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi; طفلا is a ḥāl from the object of نخرجكم. ثم لتبلغوا: a verb must be supplied, namely نعمّركم (We give you long life). لتبلغوا: the lām is for causation or for outcome, and تبلغوا is accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the wāw is the agent, and أشدكم is a mafʿūl bihi.
(وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُتَوَفَّى وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرَدُّ إِلى أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ): the wāw is a conjunction; منكم is a fronted khabar and من a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يتوفى is the ṣila; منكم is a fronted khabar and من a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause يرد is the ṣila; إلى أرذل العمر is attached to يرد. To ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib is attributed the saying that the most decrepit age is seventy-five years; it is said eighty; Qatāda said ninety. The correct view is that it is senility and dotage, and man's reaching the stage of exhaustion and feebleness, or reverting to the stage of childhood, weak in body and mind, dull of understanding.
(لِكَيْلا يَعْلَمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْئاً): لكيلا is attached to يرد; يعلم is accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and كي is maṣdar-forming [Translator's note: the author says يعلم is made accusative by an implied أن while also calling كي maṣdar-forming; as written]; من بعد علم is attached to an omitted ḥāl, because علم has the sense of عرف (to know); شيئا is the mafʿūl bihi of يعلم.
(وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ هامِدَةً فَإِذا أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهَا الْماءَ اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ وَأَنْبَتَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ): this sentence is resumptive, set out to establish the second proof. For the first proof includes what is seen and witnessed and what is not so, and so it was expressed with "creation"; whereas this proof falls within the scope of sight and is included in the class of visible things, and so it was expressed by His saying وترى (and you see). الأرض is a mafʿūl bihi, and هامدة is a ḥāl from الأرض. فإذا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is a future adverb of time containing the sense of condition; the clause أنزلنا is in a genitive construct with the adverb; عليها is attached to أنزلنا; الماء is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause اهتزت has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition; ربت is conjoined to اهتزت, and likewise His saying وأنبتت. من كل زوج is a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl bihi, that is, things and kinds being of every kind; بهيج is a naʿt of زوج.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّهُ يُحْيِ الْمَوْتى وَأَنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and بأن الله is the khabar. It is also said that ذلك is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "the matter is that", in which case the bāʾ with what follows it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. أنّ with its noun; هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; الحق is the khabar of أنّ or the khabar of هو, and the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of أنّ. وأنه is conjoined to بأن: أنّ with its noun, and the clause يحيي الموتى is its khabar. وأنه على كل شيء قدير is also conjoined. There is no harm here in citing a remark of Abū Ḥayyān, the gist of which is that the bāʾ is not causal, but rather attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "bearing witness that" (شاهد بأن); and this applies to the two aspects we mentioned above.
(وَأَنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ لا رَيْبَ فِيها): وأن الساعة is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "and the matter is that the Hour…". أنّ with its noun, and آتية is its khabar; لا is the lā of generic negation, ريب is its noun and فيها its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl, or a second khabar of أنّ.
(وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَنْ فِي الْقُبُورِ): conjoined to what precedes. أنّ with its noun, and the clause يبعث is its khabar; من is a mafʿūl bihi, and في القبور is attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila of من.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted «وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ هامِدَةً فَإِذا أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهَا الْماءَ اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ وَأَنْبَتَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ» there are rhetorical arts which the breadth of this book can hardly accommodate; we will try to summarise them as far as possible. The first of them is:

1- The combination of ṭibāq (antithesis) and takāfuʾ (equivalence):
Because one of the two opposites or one of the two counterparts comes literally and the other figuratively. The stillness of the earth (همود) and its stirring (اهتزاز) are opposites, because همود is stillness, and اهتزاز here is a particular movement, and both are figurative. Rising (الربو) and sprouting (الإنبات) are opposites, and both are literal. We said this only because the earth swells at the time the water falls upon it and does not sprout in that state; then, when the supply from the sky is cut off and the air dries the moisture of the water, the swelling subsides and the earth returns to its level state, cracks and sprouts. So the beginning of the verse is takāfuʾ, and what corresponds to it at its end is ṭibāq.
2- Irdāf (using a consequent term):
Along with these two arts it also contains the art of irdāf, which is, as Qudāma mentioned in Naqd al-Shiʿr, that the speaker intends a meaning but does not express it with the word coined for it, nor with an allusive word indicating many meanings, but with a word that is the "follower" (ردف) and consequent of the particular meaning, close to the word for the particular meaning as the rider behind is close to the rider. It was referred to earlier in (Sūrat) Hūd. Here in this verse He turned away from the literal words "movement" and "stillness" to their consequents, the words همود and اهتزاز, because the consequent words fit the intended meaning: for همود is used to mean death, and the earth, in its state of being idle without watering and vegetation, is dead land (موات), so turning to the word همود, by which death is expressed, was more fitting than the word "stillness". And the figurative اهتزاز suggests liveliness [Translator's note: the printed text reads بالعطالة ("idleness"); the context suggests liveliness or giving], like the stirring of the one praised at praise. For that reason He turned from the general word for movement to the particular word for movement, because it suggests that the earth, when watered, will give of its vegetation what pleases, by treating its watering as something that delights it, so it stirred to signal giving. Thus the benefit of turning to the consequent word has become clear, for the meanings it gives which the literal word does not give.

3- Tahdhīb (refinement):
The composition of this verse, along with what it contains of takāfuʾ, ṭibāq, irdāf and iʾtilāf, came marked by tahdhīb, because of the excellent ordering in it: the word اهتزاز precedes the word ربو, and the word ربو precedes إنبات. For when the water descends on the earth it separates its particles and enters between them; and the separation of the particles of inanimate substances is their movement at the time of the breaking of contact, because the division of a substance indicates the movement of its two parts, or one of them, from its place, and movement means nothing but this. So اهتزاز must be mentioned right after the watering, just as ربو came after اهتزاز: for when water enters soil, it rises relative to its state before that, and this is exactly ربو. It has already been explained that sprouting occurs only after the swelling and the drying of the water's moisture and the return of the soil to its state and its cracking. Thus tahdhīb is achieved in the composition of this verse through excellent ordering, and joined with that is excellent sequence, since everything that ought to be conjoined-to precedes everything that ought to be conjoined.

4- Al-madhhab al-kalāmī (the dialectical method):
In the saying of the Exalted from the beginning of Sūrat al-Ḥajj up to His saying «وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَنْ فِي الْقُبُورِ» there is the art of al-madhhab al-kalāmī. For in these verses there are five conclusions drawn from ten premises; they are set out in detail in order:
a- The saying of the Exalted «ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ»: that is because it has been established for us by mass-transmitted (mutawātir) report that He, Glorified is He, informed of the quaking of the Hour, magnifying it; and that is certain in its truth, because it is a report reported by one whose truthfulness is established, from One whose power is established, transmitted to us by mass transmission, so it is true (ḥaqq); and none informs truly of what will be except the Truth (al-Ḥaqq); so Allah is the Truth.
b- He, Glorified is He, informed that He gives life to the dead, because the Exalted informed of the terrors of the Hour as He informed, and the attainment of the benefit of this report depends on the dead being brought to life so that they witness those terrors which He, Glorified is He, has made for their sake. And it has been established that He has power over all things, and among things is giving life to the dead; so He gives life to the dead.
c- And He informed that He has power over all things, because He informed that whoever follows the devils and whoever disputes about Him without knowledge, He will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze, and none is able to do that except one who has power over all things; so He has power over all things.
d- And He informed that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, because He informed with truthful report that He created man from dust, up to His saying «لِكَيْلا يَعْلَمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْئاً», and He, Glorified is He, struck a likeness for that with the lifeless earth upon which water descends, so it stirs, swells and grows every delightful kind. And He created man as He informed: He brought him into existence by creation, then caused him not to exist by death, then will restore him by resurrection; and He brought the earth into existence after non-existence, gave it life by creation, then caused it to die by drought, then gave it life by fertility. And His report in all of that has proved true, by the evidence of the witnessed reality for the absent expected thing, until the report turned into eyewitness; His report is true.
e- In the coming of the Hour: and the Hour does not come except with the raising of those in the graves, since it is an expression for a period in which the dead rise for requital. So the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and He, Glorified is He, will raise those in the graves.

5- Majāz (figurative usage):
In the saying of the Exalted «وَأَنْبَتَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ», He attributed sprouting to the earth, and this is a rational (ʿaqlī) majāz, because the one who causes growth in reality is Allah the Exalted. The discussion of majāz has preceded more than once, and we add here that majāz is the opposite of ḥaqīqa (literal usage). Ḥaqīqa is of the pattern faʿīla in the sense of mafʿūla, from أحقّ الأمر يحقّه when he established it, or from حققته when you were certain of it. The opposite of majāz was called by that name only because it is something established and known through indication. And majāz is of the pattern mafʿal from جاز الشيء يجوزه when he passed beyond it; so when the word is turned away from what the original coinage of the language requires, it is described as majāz, meaning that they took it beyond its original place, or it passed beyond the place in which it was first coined.

The two conditions of majāz:
Majāz exists only with two conditions:
a- That the word be transferred from a meaning for which the word was first coined. By this it is distinguished from the homonymous word and from a lie that is claimed to be majāz.
b- The second condition is that the transfer be due to an affinity and connection between the origin and the branch. For that reason transferred proper names are not described as majāz; an example of that is your naming a man "Stone" (الحجر): it is said that this is majāz, and although you have transferred the name "stone" to the human being, it is a transfer for no affinity, since there is no affinity between the reality of stone and the reality of man. Whenever these two conditions are realised in a word, that word is majāz.

The two kinds of majāz:
Majāz is of two kinds: majāz of istiʿāra (metaphor) and majāz of ḥadhf (ellipsis). The first is based on simile (tashbīh), because it is making a thing (stand) for a thing for exaggeration in the simile, as in your saying "I met a lion", meaning that you met a brave man; but there is no transfer in it, as preceded, and a fuller exposition of this topic will come. So in the saying of the Exalted «وَأَنْبَتَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ», He transferred sprouting to the earth and made its greenness, freshness, abundant herbage and wondrous colours belong to it, whereas in reality all of that belongs to Allah.

dervis-irab:8-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ثانِيَ عِطْفِهِ): الثني is twisting. In al-Qāmūs: ثنى يثني الشيء means he bent it, folded it, turned part of it back onto part, and held it back. العطف is the side, which a person bends, twists and inclines when turning away from something; it is an expression by which arrogance is meant.
(حَرْفٍ): an edge; the detail of its meaning will come in the Rhetoric section.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَلا هُدىً وَلا كِتابٍ مُنِيرٍ): ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم: the discussion of it has preceded in detail, so refresh your memory of it. ولا هدى is conjoined to علم, and ولا كتاب منير is also conjoined. The discussion of the repetition of this verse will come in the Rhetoric section.
(ثانِيَ عِطْفِهِ لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): ثاني is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of يجادل. It is made accusative as a ḥāl — though a condition of the ḥāl is that it be indefinite — only because its annexation is with the intention of separation, and the nunation is intended as though pronounced. عطفه is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the "bending of the side" will be discussed in the Rhetoric section. ليضل: the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), or for outcome and consequence (al-ʿāqiba wa-l-ṣayrūra) — and perhaps this is preferable as it suits the context; يضل is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "he"; عن سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يضل, that is, from His religion.
(لَهُ فِي الدُّنْيا خِزْيٌ وَنُذِيقُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ): له is a fronted khabar (predicate); في الدنيا is a ḥāl, because it was a naʿt (adjective) of خزي and was placed before it, according to the well-known rule; خزي is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ونذيقه: the wāw is a conjunction, and نذيقه is a verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); يوم القيامة is an adverb of time attached (to it); عذاب الحريق is a second mafʿūl bihi. The clause له في الدنيا is a ḥāl.
(ذلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ يَداكَ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and بما is the khabar; the clause قدمت is the ṣila (relative clause), and يداك is the agent. وأن is conjoined to قدمت [Translator's note: as written; it is conjoined to ما], so it is in the position of genitive; أنّ with its noun, and the clause ليس is its khabar; the noun of ليس is latent, its implied form being "he"; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and ظلام is a noun genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of ليس; للعبيد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ظلام. The clause ذلك بما قدمت يداك is the speech-object of an omitted verb of saying, and the clause of saying is a ḥāl.
(وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ عَلى حَرْفٍ): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; the sentence is resumptive, set out to explain the state of those wavering in their faith and doubting their religion. من الناس is a fronted khabar; من is an indefinite qualified noun (nakira mawṣūfa), and it is a postponed mubtadaʾ, that is, qualified by an anxious worship that is neither settled nor firm, so it is exposed to whims, and the least trial or harm that befalls them blows it away. The clause يعبد الله is a naʿt of من; على حرف is a ḥāl from the agent of يعبد, that is, unsteady and wobbling. Further explanation of this expression will come in the Rhetoric section.
(فَإِنْ أَصابَهُ خَيْرٌ اطْمَأَنَّ بِهِ وَإِنْ أَصابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ انْقَلَبَ عَلى وَجْهِهِ خَسِرَ الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةَ): فإن: the fāʾ is a conjunction and إن is conditional; أصابه is a past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi and خير is the agent; اطمأن is a past verb in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); به is attached to اطمأن. وإن: the wāw conjoins to the first إن; أصابته فتنة is conjoined to what preceded; انقلب is the apodosis; على وجهه is also a ḥāl; the clause خسر الدنيا والآخرة is also a ḥāl from the agent of انقلب, and you may make it a resumptive clause or make it a badal (substitute) of the clause انقلب على وجهه. الدنيا is the object of خسر, and الآخرة is conjoined to الدنيا.
(ذلِكَ هُوَ الْخُسْرانُ الْمُبِينُ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, هو is a second mubtadaʾ, and الخسران is the khabar of هو; the clause is the khabar of ذلك; المبين is a naʿt of الخسران; the sentence is resumptive. You may make هو a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).
(يَدْعُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَضُرُّهُ وَما لا يَنْفَعُهُ ذلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلالُ الْبَعِيدُ): this clause may be a ḥāl from the agent of يعبد, and it may be resumptive. يدعو is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; من دون الله is a ḥāl; ما is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi; لا is negating, and the clause لا يضره is the ṣila; وما لا ينفعه is conjoined to the previous clause. The i'rab of the like of ذلك هو الضلال البعيد has preceded.
(يَدْعُوا لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِ لَبِئْسَ الْمَوْلى وَلَبِئْسَ الْعَشِيرُ): the clause is a badal from the previous clause يدعو, so it amounts to a repetition of it and has no grammatical position. يدعو is an imperfect verb; the lām is of commencement (ibtidāʾ), or it prepares for an oath; من is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; ضره is a second mubtadaʾ, and أقرب من نفعه is the khabar of ضره; the clause ضره أقرب من نفعه is the ṣila of من, and the clause لبئس المولى is the khabar of من. An objection to this i'rab is the entry of the lām of commencement on the khabar, which is weak with respect to the grammatical rules — unless it is said that the lām was repeated for intensification. You may make يدعو one of the verbs of the heart, containing the sense of يزعم (claims), because يزعم is speech with belief; then the clause لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, because the lām of commencement suspends (the verb) from governing it. Or يدعو has the sense of يقول (says); then من is a mubtadaʾ, ضره a second mubtadaʾ and أقرب its khabar, the clause being the ṣila of من, and the khabar of من is omitted, its implied form being إله (a god) or إلهي (my god), and the position of the clause is accusative by the (verb of) saying. The clause لبئس is resumptive, because it cannot validly enter into the quoted speech, since the unbelievers do not say of their idols "how evil a patron and how evil a companion". There is another acceptable aspect, namely that the lām is redundant on the mafʿūl bihi of يدعو. This aspect is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd): يدعو من ضره, without the lām of commencement; so من is the object of يدعو, ضره is a mubtadaʾ and أقرب a khabar, and the clause is the ṣila of من. Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī chose this aspect, and his commentators supported it. As for al-Zamakhsharī, this is the text of his statement:
"The 'far straying' is borrowed from the straying of one who has gone far into the wilderness, lost, so that the distance of his straying grew long and far. If you say: harm and benefit are denied of the idols and affirmed of them in the two verses, and this is a contradiction? I say: once the meaning is grasped, this illusion goes away. That is, Allah the Exalted declared the unbeliever foolish in that he worships an inanimate thing that possesses neither harm nor benefit, while he believes of it, in his ignorance and straying, that he will seek its intercession when he seeks its intercession. Then He said: on the Day of Resurrection this unbeliever will say, with invocation and screaming, when he sees the harm he has incurred through the idols and his entering the Fire through worshipping them, and does not see any effect of the intercession he claimed for it: «لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِ لَبِئْسَ الْمَوْلى وَلَبِئْسَ الْعَشِيرُ». Or He repeated يدعو, as though He said: he calls, he calls upon, besides Allah, what neither harms him nor benefits him; then He said: «لمن ضره» — by its being worshipped — «is nearer than its benefit» — by its being an intercessor — «how evil a patron». And in the reading (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh: من ضره, without a lām."
So it is as though al-Zamakhsharī, may Allah have mercy on him, summarised the i'rab analyses we have cited, although there are numerous aspects that the commentators have followed, exceeding seven, but all of them are far from logic. We cite for you one of them by way of example, the view of al-Farrāʾ; he said: "The implied form is يدعو من لضره (he calls upon one whose harm…); then the lām was placed before its position." The arbitrariness in it is not hidden, as is the placing of what is in the ṣila of الذي before it.
There is a view no less strange and anomalous than this, namely that ذلك has the sense of الذي, in the position of accusative by يدعو, that is: he calls upon that which is the straying; but the object was fronted. This proceeds on the view of whoever makes ذا, without interrogation, have the sense of الذي, although it is confined to your saying ماذا and من ذا? And there is another, even more impossible, view, namely that the implied form is: ذلك هو الضلال البعيد يدعوه; so ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, هو a second mubtadaʾ, or a badal, or a pronoun of separation, الضلال the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and يدعوه a ḥāl, the implied form being مدعوًّا (being called upon). It is an aspect that, as you see, condemns itself as feeble. We cited these views only to arrive at the statement that this verse is among the difficult passages that have occupied the scholars of grammar and exegesis, and they have not produced anything in it that quenches thirst; and the inimitable speech of Allah is too lofty to be reached by the rules that man has laid down.
بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; المولى is the agent, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "it". ولبئس العشير is conjoined to His saying لبئس المولى.

dervis-irab:14-17.t:
