(وَلَوْلا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ لَهُدِّمَتْ صَوامِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَواتٌ وَمَساجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا اسْمُ اللَّهِ كَثِيراً): the wāw is resumptive; لولا is a particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence, containing the sense of condition. دفع الله is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is obligatorily omitted; الناس is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of دفع, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its agent, which is الله. The meaning is: were it not that Allah repels people by means of one another, the corrupters would prevail and the interests (of people) would be disrupted. Its opposite is rare in usage, namely that the maṣdar be annexed to its object and then its agent come in the nominative, as in the saying of al-Uqayshir al-Asadī:
أفنى تلادي وما جمعت من نشب ... قرع القواقيز أفواه الأباريق
(The knocking of the mouths of the ewers against the drinking-cups has consumed my inherited wealth and the property I gathered.)
قرع, with qāf and undotted ʿayn, is nominative as the agent of أفنى; it is a maṣdar annexed to its object, which is القواقيز — with two qāfs and a dotted zāy: cups from which wine is drunk; its singular is قاقوزة, with two dotted zāys [Translator's note: as written; قاقوزة has one zāy], so its plural is قوازيز [Translator's note: as written; the word in the verse is قواقيز]. أفواه is the agent of the maṣdar; it is the plural of فم, whose origin is فوه, and that is why (the hāʾ) is restored in the plural. However, the verse is also narrated with الأفواه in the accusative, in which case it is of the first kind.
بعضهم is a badal of part (badal baʿḍ) of الناس; ببعض is attached to دفع. The lām occurs in the apodosis of لولا; هدمت is a passive past verb; صوامع is the nāʾib fāʿil; بيع, صلوات and مساجد are conjoined to صوامع. The mention of the mosques was put last because hermitages, synagogues and churches are older in existence than they. The clause يذكر is a naʿt of the places mentioned; فيها is attached to يذكر; اسم الله is the nāʾib fāʿil; كثيرا is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, that is, much remembrance; or a naʿt of an omitted adverb, that is, much time.
(وَلَيَنْصُرَنَّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām prepares for an oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); ينصرن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis. الله is the agent; من is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi; the clause ينصره is the ṣila. The clause of إنّ and what follows it is an emphasis of the reason for the help: الله is its noun, the lām is the shifted lām, قوي is its first khabar and عزيز its second khabar.
(الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكاةَ وَأَمَرُوا بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهَوْا عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ): الذين is a badal of the preceding الذين, or a second naʿt of the first الذين, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. You have another aspect, namely to parse it as a badal of «من ينصره»; al-Zajjāj mentioned this aspect; he said: that is, Allah will surely help those who, if We establish them… إن is conditional; مكناهم is a past verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi, and it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); في الأرض is attached to مكناهم; أقاموا is a past verb and agent, and it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); الصلاة is a mafʿūl bihi, and what follows is conjoined to it.
(وَلِلَّهِ عاقِبَةُ الْأُمُورِ): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; لله is a fronted khabar, and عاقبة الأمور a postponed mubtadaʾ.

* Benefits:
Jihad is the peak of the hump of Islam:
The hadiths on jihad are many; we cite from them what rises to the peak of eloquence, following our method in this book. From Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "Which deed is best?" He said: "Faith in Allah and His Messenger." It was said: "Then what?" He said: "Jihad in the path of Allah." It was said: "Then what?" He said: "An accepted (mabrūr) pilgrimage." Narrated by al-Bukhārī, Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Khuzayma in his Ṣaḥīḥ.
And from Muʿādh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with the people before the expedition of Tabūk. When morning came, he led the people in the dawn prayer; then the people mounted. When the sun rose, the people grew drowsy after the night journey, and Muʿādh kept close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, following in his track, while the people's mounts had scattered with them along the main roads, grazing and moving on. While Muʿādh was following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and his she-camel was grazing at one time and moving on at another, Muʿādh's she-camel stumbled, so he jerked her jaw with the rein, and she sprang up so that the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shied from her. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ removed his head-covering and turned, and there was no one in the army nearer to him than Muʿādh. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him and said: "O Muʿādh." He said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Come closer." So he drew near to us [Translator's note: as written; "to him" seems intended] until their two mounts were touching one another. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I did not think the people were so far from us as they are." Muʿādh said: "O Prophet of Allah, the people grew drowsy, so their mounts scattered, grazing and moving on." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And I too was drowsy." When Muʿādh saw the cheerfulness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his being alone with him, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to ask you about a matter that has made me ill, made me sick and saddened me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask about whatever you wish." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, tell me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise; I will not ask you about anything else." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bravo, bravo, bravo! You have asked about something tremendous" — three times — "and it is easy for one for whom Allah wills good; and it is easy for one for whom Allah wills good; and it is easy for one for whom Allah wills good." And he did not tell him anything without the Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeating it three times, out of eagerness that he should learn it well from him. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "You believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish the prayer, pay the zakāt, and worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him, until you die while you are upon that." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, repeat it for me," so he repeated it three times. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "If you wish, O Muʿādh, I will tell you of the head of this matter, the pillar of this matter, and the peak of the hump?" Muʿādh said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah; tell me, may my father and mother be your ransom." The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "The head of this matter is that you bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger; the pillar of this matter is establishing the prayer and paying the zakāt; and the peak of its hump is jihad in the path of Allah. I have only been commanded to fight people until they establish the prayer, pay the zakāt, and bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger; when they have done that, they have held fast and protected their blood and their property, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, no face has grown pale and no foot has become dusty in a deed by which the ranks of the Hereafter are sought, after the obligatory prayer, like jihad in the path of Allah; and nothing has made a servant's scale heavy like a mount spent in the path of Allah or ridden in the path of Allah."

dervis-irab:75-78.t:
* I'rab:
(اللَّهُ يَصْطَفِي مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ رُسُلًا وَمِنَ النَّاسِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ) A resumptive clause brought to establish His, Exalted is He, choosing of the messengers. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (يصطفي) the khabar (predicate); (من الملائكة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of (رسلا) and was placed before it; you may also attach it to (يصطفي). (رسلا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من الناس) is conjoined to (من الملائكة), and [the object] is omitted from the second because the first indicates it, i.e. and He chooses messengers from among people. The clause (إن الله سميع بصير) gives the reason for what preceded, i.e. All-Hearing of what they say, All-Seeing of whom He takes as a messenger; (إن) and its noun; (سميع) is its first khabar and (بصير) its second khabar. (يَعْلَمُ ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَما خَلْفَهُمْ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ) The clause (يعلم) is a third khabar, or resumptive. (يعلم) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He"; (ما) is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi; (بين أيديهم): the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause); (وما خلفهم) is conjoined to (ما بين أيديهم). (وإلى الله): the wāw is a conjunction, and (إلى الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ترجع); (ترجع) is an imperfect passive verb and (الأمور) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ارْكَعُوا وَاسْجُدُوا وَاعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ) The iʿrāb of (يا أيها الذين آمنوا) has been given before; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila. (اركعوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (اسجدوا) is conjoined to (اركعوا), and (اعبدوا ربكم) is also conjoined. (وَافْعَلُوا الْخَيْرَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ) (وافعلوا الخير) is conjoined to what preceded; the clause (لعلكم تفلحون) is a ḥāl of the wāw in (اركعوا) and what is conjoined to it, i.e. do these things while hoping for success. (وَجاهِدُوا فِي اللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهادِهِ) (وجاهدوا) is also conjoined; (في الله) is attached to (جاهدوا), and there must be an omitted muḍāf, after the omission of the object of (جاهدوا), i.e. strive against your enemies for the sake of Allah and on His account; so (في) is causal. (حق جهاده) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(هُوَ اجْتَباكُمْ وَما جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ) (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (اجتباكم), i.e. He chose you, is the khabar; the clause is a ḥāl of (الله). (وما): the wāw is a conjunction and (ما) is negative; (جعل) is a past verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "He"; (عليكم) is attached to an omitted second object of (جعل); (في الدين) is a ḥāl; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (حرج) is genitive in form and accusative in position, because it is the first object of (جعل).
(مِلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْراهِيمَ هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَفِي هذا) There are several aspects for the accusative of (ملة), the most evident being what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned; his text is: «The milla is put in the accusative by the content of what precedes it, as if it were said: He has made your religion wide, with the widening of the milla of your father; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. It may also be put in the accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), i.e. by the religion I specially mean the milla of your father»; or by an implied verb, its implied form being "follow". There are other aspects that do not go beyond these. (أبيكم) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and (إبراهيم) is a badal (substitute) of (أبيكم). (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (سماكم) the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl of (إبراهيم); (سماكم) is a verb, a latent fāʿil and the first object, and (المسلمين) is the second object; (من قبل) is a ḥāl, i.e. before this Book, and (وفي هذا) is conjoined to (من قبل), i.e. and in this Qur'an.
(لِيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ شَهِيداً عَلَيْكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا شُهَداءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ) The lām is causal, and it is said it is of consequence (ʿāqiba); (يكون) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (أن) after the lām; the lām and what it governs are attached to (سماكم). (الرسول) is the noun of (يكون) and (شهيدا) the khabar of (يكون); (عليكم) is attached to (شهيدا); (وتكونوا شهداء على الناس) is conjoined to its counterpart. (فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِاللَّهِ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa); (أقيموا الصلاة) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and what follows is conjoined to it. (هُوَ مَوْلاكُمْ فَنِعْمَ الْمَوْلى وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ) The clause is a ḥāl of (الله); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (مولاكم) the khabar. (فنعم المولى): the fāʾ is resumptive; (نعم) is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise; (المولى) is the fāʿil, and the one specified for praise is omitted, i.e. "He"; (ونعم النصير) is conjoined to (نعم المولى).

dervis-irab:42-46.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِئْرٍ): in al-Mukhtār: "بأر بئرا, with a hamza after the bāʾ: he dug it; of the pattern قطع [Translator's note: printed as ربابه قطع; من باب قطع is evidently meant]." البئر is of the pattern فِعْل in the sense of مفعول, like الذبح in the sense of المذبوح: a large pit in the ground from which water is drawn; the plural is آبار, أبآر, بئار and أبؤر, and it is feminine. In al-Asās: "The great sinner is one who ابتأر, and the petty sinner one who ابتهر. One says: ابتأرت الجارية when he says 'I did it with her' and he is truthful, and ابتهرتها when he says that and he is lying. Al-Kumayt recited:
قبيح بمثلي نعت الفتا ... ة إما ابتهارا وإما ابتئارا
(It is ugly for one like me to describe a young woman, whether by lying boast or by true confession.)"
(مُعَطَّلَةٍ): abandoned through the death of its people, although it is in working order, with water in it and the tools for drawing water with it.
(مَشِيدٍ): raised high, plastered; from شاد البناء, that is, he raised it; one also says شيّد. In al-Nisāʾ it came from شيّد [Translator's note: as written; the reference is to مشيّدة in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:78], because there it occurred after a plural, whereas here it occurred after a singular, so the light form suited it.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَعادٌ وَثَمُودُ): the wāw is resumptive; the sentence is resumptive, set out to console the Prophet ﷺ, and (to show) that he is not unique in being given the lie. إن is conditional; يكذبوك is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the wāw is the agent and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). فقد: the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is joined with قد; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); كذبت is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; the clause is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). قبلهم is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) كذبت; قوم نوح is the agent; عاد and ثمود are conjoined to قوم. قوم was treated as feminine with regard to the meaning of "nation" or "tribe". He did not say "the people of ʿĀd and Thamūd", dispensing with it because they are well known by these two names.
(وَقَوْمُ إِبْراهِيمَ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ): conjoined to what precedes.
(وَأَصْحابُ مَدْيَنَ وَكُذِّبَ مُوسى فَأَمْلَيْتُ لِلْكافِرِينَ): وأصحاب مدين is conjoined. He turned away from "the people of Shuʿayb" because the people of Madyan were more deeply rooted in giving the lie than the people of the Thicket (al-Ayka); that is why He singled them out for mention. كذب is a passive past verb, and موسى is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). He varied the speech and did not say "the people of Mūsā", because, having opened the speech by recounting their giving the lie, then enumerated the kinds of those who gave the lie and their groups, and having reached Mūsā only after the speech had grown long, it was good to repeat it so that it would immediately precede His saying فأمليت, and so the effect would be joined to the cause — just as He said in the verse of (Sūrat) Qāf after enumerating them: «كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ», thus linking the punishment and the threat and joining them to the giving of the lie after renewing mention of it. فأمليت: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أمليت is a verb and agent; للكافرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أمليت.
(ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهُمْ فَكَيْفَ كانَ نَكِيرِ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with an interval; أخذتهم is a verb, an agent and a mafʿūl bihi. فكيف: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; نكير is the noun of كان, that is, إنكاري (My disapproval), and the yāʾ was dropped. النكير is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of disapproval and changing (things), since He replaced their blessing with punishment, their life with destruction, and their building with ruin. The meaning of the interrogative will come in the Rhetoric section.
(فَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْناها وَهِيَ ظالِمَةٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive; the sentence is resumptive, set out to confirm what preceded by striking examples and citing evidence. كأين is predicative (khabariyya, "how many"), and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); من قرية is the tamyīz (specification) of كأين, and its verification has preceded. The clause أهلكناها, consisting of verb, agent and mafʿūl bihi, is the khabar of كأين. It is permissible for كأين to be accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), by an omitted verb explained by أهلكناها, in which case the clause أهلكناها is explicative. وهي ظالمة: the wāw is circumstantial; هي is a mubtadaʾ and ظالمة a khabar; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(فَهِيَ خاوِيَةٌ عَلى عُرُوشِها وَبِئْرٍ مُعَطَّلَةٍ وَقَصْرٍ مَشِيدٍ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; هي is a mubtadaʾ and خاوية a khabar; the clause is conjoined to the clause أهلكناها. على عروشها is either attached to خاوية, in which case the meaning is that it has fallen down upon its roofs, that is, its roofs collapsed to the ground, then its walls were demolished and fell on top of the roofs; or it is a second khabar of هي, as though it were said: it is empty, and it is upon its roofs, that is, standing, overlooking its roofs, meaning that the roofs fell to the ground and came to be in line with the walls, and the walls remained standing, stark, looking down on the fallen roofs. Both estimations are beautiful and admissible. بئر is conjoined to قرية, that is, and how many a well; معطلة is a naʿt (adjective) of بئر; وقصر مشيد is also conjoined. Whether it is a specific well and a specific palace, or whether the two occur by way of a likeness — the discussion of all this will come in the Benefits section.
(أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌ يَعْقِلُونَ بِها أَوْ آذانٌ يَسْمَعُونَ بِها): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī) if they had travelled, or for urging travel so that they may see the places where those before them fell. The fāʾ conjoins to an implied element required by the context, that is: did they neglect and disregard, and travel and not benefit? لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past meaning) and jussivisation; يسيروا is an imperfect verb made jussive by لم, and the wāw is its agent; في الأرض is attached to يسيروا. فتكون: the fāʾ is causal, and تكون is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the causal fāʾ; لهم is the fronted khabar of تكون, and قلوب its postponed noun; the clause يعقلون is a naʿt of قلوب, and بها is attached to يعقلون. أو is a conjunction, and آذان is conjoined to قلوب; the clause يسمعون بها is a naʿt of آذان. It is clear that what is derived from the negated also entails negation.
(فَإِنَّها لا تَعْمَى الْأَبْصارُ وَلكِنْ تَعْمَى الْقُلُوبُ الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ): the fāʾ is for causation; إنّ with its noun, the pronoun referring to the story or the matter (al-qiṣṣa aw al-shaʾn); the clause لا تعمى الأبصار is the khabar. ولكن: the wāw is a conjunction, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), made inoperative because it is lightened; تعمى القلوب is an imperfect verb and agent; التي is a naʿt of القلوب; في الصدور is attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The secret of His saying في الصدور will come in the Rhetoric section.

* Rhetoric:
1- The interrogative in the saying of the Exalted «فَكَيْفَ كانَ نَكِيرِ» means affirmation (taqrīr), which is leading the addressee to acknowledge what he knows but disputes, resorting to obstinacy and sophistry in opposing it. Abū Ḥayyān said: "This interrogative is accompanied by the sense of wonder, as though it were said: how severe was My disapproval of them!" And this too is clear; so the interrogative is, then, for affirmation with wonder.
2- Infiṣāl (anticipating and resolving an objection) in the saying of the Exalted «وَلكِنْ تَعْمَى الْقُلُوبُ الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ». For someone might say: hearts are only ever in the breasts, so what benefit is there in mentioning what is familiar and existent, since it is known? The resolution of that is to say: what is familiar is that real blindness has its place in the eyesight, because it is the affliction of the pupil with what effaces its light, and its use for the heart is figurative (majāz). So when it was intended to transfer it from the literal to the figurative, the speech amounted to affirming what is contrary to the familiar and to the original, so it needed additional specification, so that it would be established that blindness has its place in the hearts, not in the eyes. It is as when you say: "Sharpness does not belong to the sword, but to your tongue which is between your jaws": your saying "between your jaws" establishes what you have claimed for his tongue and the denial of sharpness of the sword, which is the familiar. This is among the rare gems of eloquence, so understand it. The upshot of the matter is that the defect is not in their senses, for they are sound with no fault in them; rather the defect is in their relapsed intellects and their disabled minds.

* Benefits:
The abandoned well and the lofty palace: it is said that they are specific. Al-Khaṭīb al-Shirbīnī said in his tafsīr: "It is narrated that this well is the one at which Ṣāliḥ alighted with four thousand persons of those who believed in him, and Allah the Exalted saved them from the punishment; it is in Ḥaḍramawt, and it was so called only because Ṣāliḥ was present (حضر) at it when he died. And there, at the well [Translator's note: printed as عبد البئر; عند البئر seems intended], is a town named Ḥāḍūrā, which the people of Ṣāliḥ built; they appointed over themselves Julhus ibn Julās and dwelt there for a time; then they disbelieved and worshipped an idol, and Allah sent to them Ḥanẓala ibn Ṣafwān as a prophet, but they killed him, so Allah the Exalted destroyed them, abandoned their well and ruined their palaces." The preferable view is that the well is general and the palace is general, that is: how many a town We have destroyed, how many a well We have left idle, without those who draw from it, and how many a lofty palace whose people have dispersed from it and whose inhabitants have moved away from it.

dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَرِيدٍ): insolent, stripped bare for corruption. al-Zajjāj said: al-marīd and al-mārid is the one who is high and smooth. And it is said in al-Qāmūs and its commentary: al-mārid is the insolent, the lofty; one says "a mārid building", i.e. a lofty one, and this is figurative (majāz); its plural is maradah, māridūn and murrād. And al-marīd is the one intense in defiance, the vile and wicked; its plural is murd and its feminine is mardāʾ. One says: "murd on jurd", i.e. beardless youths on short-haired horses.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ شَيْءٌ عَظِيمٌ) يا is a particle of vocative; أَيُّهَا is an indefinite, specified vocative (munādā nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is for alerting; النَّاسُ is a badal (substitute) for أَيُّ in wording; اتَّقُوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable by omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ: إنّ and its noun; شَيْءٌ is its khabar and عَظِيمٌ an adjective of شَيْءٌ; the clause إنّ زلزلة الساعة etc. is causal and has no grammatical position, owing to His saying اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ. And زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ is the annexation of the maṣdar to its agent or to its object. On the first, it is as though the Hour itself were what shakes things, by figurative attribution (majāz ḥukmī); on the second, it follows the way of extension in the adverbial, treating it as a direct object, like His saying «بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ». (يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَها تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ عَمَّا أَرْضَعَتْ وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَها)
The adverbial is attached to تَذْهَلُ, and the clause تَرَوْنَها is the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverbial. They allowed other possibilities for it, among them that it be attached to عَظِيمٌ, or to an implied اذْكُرْ ("remember"), or that it be a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) of زَلْزَلَةَ, since each of the event and the time can be said to include the other. The pronoun in تَرَوْنَها refers to the Hour, i.e. the Resurrection, since it is of such a degree as to cut the vessels of the hearts; it may also refer to the earthquake (zalzala), and perhaps this is nearer since it is in this world. تَذْهَلُ is a nominative imperfect verb; كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ is the agent; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of تَرَوْنَها, i.e. the hāʾ — for the seeing here is certainly by sight. This holds if we do not make يَوْمَ attached to تَذْهَلُ; if it is attached to it, the ḥāl is not allowed and the clause becomes resumptive, or else it is a ḥāl from the earthquake, or from the latent pronoun in عَظِيمٌ, or from the Hour even though it is a muḍāf ilayhi, because it is either an agent or a direct object, as stated above. In that case an omitted pronoun must be implied, i.e. "she is distracted in it". The murḍiʿa (with tāʾ marbūṭa) is the one actually engaged in nursing, having put her breast in the infant's mouth, whereas the murḍiʿ (without it) is the one whose nature it is to nurse, whether she is actually nursing or not; so they distinguished between the two with the tāʾ marbūṭa. More detail on this secret will come in the chapter on rhetoric. عَمَّا أَرْضَعَتْ is attached to تَذْهَلُ, and ما is a relative or a maṣdar particle, i.e. "from that which she nursed" or "from her nursing". وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ: an imperfect verb and an agent, and the clause is conjoined to the clause تَذْهَلُ; ذاتِ حَمْلٍ is a muḍāf to كُلُّ and حَمْلَها is the direct object of تَضَعُ. al-ḥamL with fatḥa on the unpointed ḥāʾ is what is in the belly or on a tree, and with kasra it is what is on the back. (وَتَرَى النَّاسَ سُكارى وَما هُمْ بِسُكارى وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ)
The wāw is a conjunction; تَرَى is an imperfect verb conjoined to تَرَوْنَها. It is plural in the first and singular in the second only because the first seeing is tied to the earthquake or the Hour, which all people see, whereas the second is tied to people being drunk, so each person must be made a seer of the rest, disregarding his own being described as drunk. The agent of تَرَى is latent, its implied form being "you"; النَّاسَ is a direct object; سُكارى is a ḥāl; the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl; ما is a negative in the Ḥijāzī manner; هُمْ is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and سُكارى is genitive in wording and accusative in position as the khabar of ما; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from النَّاسَ. Both ḍamma and fatḥa are possible on the sīn of سُكارى — they are two dialects, and it has been read with both. As for وَلكِنَّ, the wāw is a conjunction on an omitted element, contrasting with what follows لكنّ, and this is a regular ruling for it. The implied form, as in al-Baḥr of Abū Ḥayyān: «These states — the distraction, the delivering, and seeing people like the drunk — are mild and gentle, but the punishment of Allah is severe, i.e. not gentle and not easy; so what follows لكنّ contrasts with what precedes it.» More discussion of this verse will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to mention the one who was heedless of the recompense in that and denied it; the connection between it and what precedes of the mention of the terrors of the Hour and its earthquake is plain. مِنَ النَّاسِ is a fronted khabar; مَنْ is certainly an indefinite described noun, and it is a delayed mubtadaʾ, i.e. people described by disputation, obstinacy, sophistry and stubborn arrogance, among whom admonitions are of no use and proofs have no effect. The clause يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ is an adjective of مَنْ, and the pronoun is singular in regard to the wording of مَنْ; had it been plural in regard to its meaning, it would have been permissible. فِي اللَّهِ is attached to يُجادِلُ, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "His power, His attributes and His religion". بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ is a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in يُجادِلُ, i.e. ignorant, stumbling in the wildernesses of blind misguidance and abominable ignorance. (وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطانٍ مَرِيدٍ) وَيَتَّبِعُ is conjoined to يُجادِلُ; كُلَّ is a direct object; شَيْطانٍ is a muḍāf ilayhi; and مَرِيدٍ
is an adjective of شَيْطانٍ; an omitted muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "the footsteps of every devil". (كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ مَنْ تَوَلَّاهُ فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ وَيَهْدِيهِ إِلى عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ) كُتِبَ is a passive past verb; عَلَيْهِ is attached to it; أنّ and what is within its scope is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil; مَنْ is a jussive conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ — it is also possible that مَنْ be a relative noun and a mubtadaʾ with فَأَنَّهُ as the khabar, the fāʾ having entered because of the scent of condition in the relative; the clause يُضِلُّهُ is the khabar of أنّه, and the clause of the condition or the relative is the khabar of أنّه. al-Zamakhsharī allowed that فَأَنَّهُ be conjoined to the first, and Abū Ḥayyān took him to task, saying: this is not allowed, because if you make فَأَنَّهُ conjoined to أنّه, then أنّه is left without a complete khabar. Yet many have supported al-Zamakhsharī in his i'rab, and we see that what we have chosen is nearer to the correct. وَيَهْدِيهِ is conjoined to يُضِلُّهُ, and إِلى عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ is attached to يَهْدِيهِ.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «وَتَرَى النَّاسَ سُكارى وَما هُمْ بِسُكارى»
is a tashbīh baligh (eloquent simile), for He likened the people on that harsh day to the state of the drunk, who have lost discrimination and squandered right guidance. The scholars say: among the proofs of figurative speech is that its contrary can truthfully be said, as in your saying "Zayd is a donkey" when you describe him as dull and stupid, and then it is true to say "he is not a donkey", denying him the literal sense. Likewise the verse, after affirming figurative drunkenness, denied the literal sense with the most emphatic denial, strengthened by the bāʾ. The secret of its emphasis is to alert that this drunkenness that is upon them in that state is nothing of the familiar kind, but is a matter they had never known the like of before. And the rectification (istidrāk) by His saying «وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ»
returns to His saying وما هم بسكارى, and it is as though it were an explanation for affirming the figurative drunkenness, as if it were said: If they are not drunk from wine, which is the familiar drunkenness, what then is this strange drunkenness, and what is its cause? So it was said: the severity of the punishment of Allah the Exalted.
2- In His turning from murḍiʿ to murḍiʿa there is a secret few perceive. It is that the murḍiʿa is the one who has actually been nursing, so her pulling her breast from her child's mouth when the terror occurs is more indicative of bewilderment, and a fuller embodiment of the places of distraction that overcame her. There is another difference: the form that comes by attribution (nasab), i.e. murḍiʿ, takes no account of the occurrence of the attribute from which it is derived, but implies that its subject is described by it; whereas the form not by attribution, i.e. murḍiʿa, takes account of the occurrence of the act and the attribute's issuing from it. And this is among the secrets of our language that are rare in other languages.
And it is said in al-Mufaṣṣal: «The doctrine of the Kufans is that the tāʾ is omitted from ḥāʾiḍ because it is dispensed with, and this requires the tāʾ to be kept where there is ambiguity, as in ḍāmir, ʿāshiq, ayyim, thayyib and ʿānis.» This objection is clear. As for the objection from the retention of the tāʾ in attributes specific to females, such as imraʾa maʿība and kalba mujriya according to al-Ṣiḥāḥ, it is not sound, because what they mentioned is permitted, not required, for they say that bringing the tāʾ where it can be dispensed with is the original, like ḥāmila for the woman. It is said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: One says imraʾa ḥāmil and ḥāmila when she is pregnant; whoever says ḥāmil says this is an adjective, and whoever says ḥāmila builds it on "ḥamalat, so she is ḥāmila". And he recited a verse of ʿAmr ibn Ḥassān:
تمخضت المنون له بيوم ... أتى ولكل حاملة تمام
(Fate was in labour for him with a day that came; and every pregnant one has her term.)
But if she carries something on her back or on her head, she is ḥāmila and nothing else.

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَافِعُ﴾ — and (يَدْفع) also. Most of the Readers read (يدافع), and that is how I read. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (يدافع), and (وَلَو لاَ دِفَاعُ الله); and each of them is correct.

farraa:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَاتَلُونَ﴾ — also (يقاتِلوُن). Its meaning is: Allah has given permission to those who fight, that they may fight; this was when ﴿فَاقْتُلوُا المُشْرِكينَ حيثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ was revealed. It was also read ﴿أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا﴾, and the meaning is: permission has been given them to fight. Each of them is correct.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُواْ مِن دِيَارِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ﴾ — He is saying: they were expelled only for their saying "There is no god but Allah". If you wish, you may make His saying ﴿لاَّ أَن يَقُولُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ﴾ in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), referring it back to the bāʾ in (بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ); and if you wish, you may make (أن) the excepted (mustathnā), as He said: ﴿إلاَّ ابْتغاء وَجْهِ ربِّه الأعلى﴾.
His saying: ﴿لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَامِعُ وَبِيَعٌ﴾ — these [the biyaʿ] are the places of prayer of the Christians, and the ṣawāmiʿ (cloisters) are for the monks. As for the ṣalawāt, they are the synagogues of the Jews, and the masājid are (the mosques of Islam). The meaning of the demolishing is that Allah said before that: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ — He repels, by His command and by its followers, [harm] from the religion of every prophet, until Allah sent Muḥammad ﷺ.

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿فَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَبِئْرٍ مُّعَطَّلَةٍ وَقَصْرٍ مَّشِيدٍ﴾ — the well and the palace are put in the genitive (khafḍ) by conjunction (ʿaṭf) with the roofs (العروش). Yet when you consider its meaning, you find that (عَلَى) does not fit well with them, because the roofs are the tops of the houses, whereas the well is in the ground, and likewise the palace, since the town did not collapse onto the palace. Rather, one part was made to follow another, as He said: ﴿وَحُورٍ عينٍ كأَمْثَالِ اللُؤْلُؤ﴾. And if you put the well «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 122b]» and the palace in the genitive — intending that they are not part of the town — by means of من, it would be as if you said: How many a town has been destroyed, and how many a well and how many a palace. The first is dearer to me.

farraa:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِنَّهَا لاَ تَعْمَى ٱلأَبْصَارُ﴾ — the hāʾ is (a hāʾ of ʿimād, a support pronoun) by which إنّ is given its due. (إنَّه) is permissible in its place, and that is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (فانه لا تعمى الأبصَار ولكن تعمى القلوب التى فى الصّدور). The heart is only ever in the breast; it is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the kind the Arabs add to a meaning already known, as it was said: ﴿فصِيَامُ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فى الحَجِّ وسَبْعَةٍ إذا رَجَعتُم تِلْكَ عَشَرةٌ كامِلَةٌ﴾, and it is known that three and seven make ten. Similar to that is: "I looked at you with my own eye". Similar to it is the saying of Allah: ﴿يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ مَا لَيْسَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم﴾, and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿إنَّ هَذَا أَخِى لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُون نَعْجَةً وَلِى نَعْجَةٌ أٌنْثَى﴾; this too is emphasis. And if someone says: ﴿كيف انْصرَف من العذاب﴾ «[Translator's note: i.e. "How did it turn away from the punishment"]» to the point where He said: ﴿وإنَّ يوماً عند رَبِّك﴾? The answer to that is that they sought to hasten the punishment in this world, so Allah revealed to His Prophet: ﴿وَلَنْ يُخْلِفَ اللهُ وَعْدَهُ﴾, that is, in sending the punishment down upon them in this world. So His saying ﴿وَإِنَّ يَوْماً عند رَبِّك﴾ is also about their punishment. Thus it is consistent: they are punished in this world, and in the Hereafter more severely.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ يَوْماً عِندَ رَبِّكَ كَأَلْفِ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ﴾.
It is said: a day of the days of their punishment in the Hereafter is like a thousand years of what you count in this world.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿مُعَاجِزِينَ﴾ — the reading of the general public is (مُعَاجِزِينَ), and the meaning of muʿājizīn is "obstinately opposing". The entry of (فى) is as when you say: "I strove in your affair", meaning: I intended good or evil for you. Mujāhid and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr read (معجِّزينَ), meaning: hindering [others].

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ وَلاَ نَبِيٍّ إِلاَّ﴾ — the messenger (rasūl) is the prophet who is sent, and the prophet (nabī) is the one spoken to [by inspiration] who has not been sent.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰ﴾ — al-tamannī is recitation, and also talking to oneself.

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿فَتُصْبِحُ ٱلأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً﴾ — you put (فتُصبح) in the nominative (rafʿ) because the meaning of ﴿أَلَم تر﴾ is a statement (khabar), as though you said in ordinary speech: Know that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes [green]. It is like the poet's saying:
أَلم تسأل الربع القديم فينطق * فهل تُخبرنكَ اليوم بَيْداءٌ سَمْلَق
(Did you not ask the old encampment, and it speaks? — but will a barren desert tell you anything today?)
that is: you have asked it, and it spoke. Had you made it a question and made the fāʾ [introduce] a condition, you would put it in the accusative (naṣb), as another said:
أَلَم تسأل فتخبرَك الديارا * عن الحىّ المضلَّل حيث سَارَا
(Will you not ask, so that the abodes may tell you of the misguided tribe, where it has gone?)
The jussive (jazm) is also permissible in this verse, as he said:
فقلت له صَوِّب ولا تجهدَنَّه * فيُذرك من أخرى العَطاةِ فَتزلق
(I said to him: "Bring it down gently and do not overtax it, lest it throw you from the rear of the [mount] and you slip.")
for he made the answer with the fāʾ as though it were coordinated with what precedes it.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿مَنسَكاً﴾ and ﴿مَنْسِكاً﴾ — it has been read both ways. Mansik is [the usage] of the people of the Ḥijāz and mansak of the Banū Asad. Al-mansak in the speech of the Arabs is the place you frequent habitually and are attached to; it is said: "So-and-so has a mansik that he frequents", whether in good or otherwise. The rites (al-manāsik) were named after that — and Allah knows best — because people keep returning to them for the Ḥajj and the ʿUmra.

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿يَكَادُونَ يَسْطُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَٰتِنَا﴾ — He means the idolaters of the people of Mecca: whenever they heard a man «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 213a]» of the Muslims reciting the Qurʾān, they nearly assaulted him.
His saying: ﴿ٱلنَّارُ وَعَدَهَا ٱللَّهُ﴾ — you put it in the nominative because it is a definite noun explaining الشرّ (the worse), which is indefinite; as you say: "I passed by two men — your father and your brother". Had you put it in the accusative by means of what refers back to it [the pronoun in وعدها], intending to connect it with what precedes, it would be a valid way. And had you put it in the genitive by the bāʾ — ﴿فأنبئكم بشرّ من ذلكم بالنار﴾ — it would be correct. But the [preferred] way is the nominative.

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلطَّالِبُ وَٱلْمَطْلُوبُ﴾ — the seeker is the gods, and the sought is the fly. It carries the sense of a parable.

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿مَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾ — that is, they did not magnify Allah as He truly deserves to be magnified. It is as you say in ordinary speech: "You did not recognise so-and-so's worth (qadr)", that is, his greatness, and his companion fell short in his regard.

farraa:75-75.t: His saying: ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَصْطَفِي مِنَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةِ رُسُلاً﴾ — He chose from among them Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl, the Angel of Death and their like; and He chooses from among mankind the prophets.

farraa:77-77.t: His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱرْكَعُواْ وَٱسْجُدُواْ﴾ — people used to prostrate without bowing, so they were commanded that their prayer should have a bowing before the prostration.

farraa:78-78.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ﴾ — [ḥaraj means] constriction.
His saying: ﴿مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ﴾ — you put it in the accusative on the sense: He has made it wide for you like the religion (milla) of your father Ibrāhīm; because His saying ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ﴾ means: He made it wide and easy like the religion of Ibrāhīm; so when you drop the kāf, you put it in the accusative. ﴿مِلَّةَ إبراهيم﴾ may also be put in the accusative as a command to [follow] it, because the beginning of the passage is a command, as though He said: Bow, and hold fast to the religion of Ibrāhīm.
His saying: ﴿مِن قَبْلُ وَفِي هَـٰذَا﴾ — He means the Qurʾān.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ﴾: the readers put (كلُّ مُرْضِعَة) in the nominative because they made the verb belong to it. Had it been said "tudhhilu kulla murḍiʿatin" (accusative), meaning that the Hour makes its people distracted, it would have been a valid option, but I have not heard anyone read it so. Al-murḍiʿa is the mother; al-murḍiʿ is the woman who has a child with her whom she suckles. Were murḍiʿ said of the mother — since suckling only comes from females — it would be like your saying ṭāmith and ḥāʾiḍ ("menstruating", without the feminine ending). And had murḍiʿa been said of the one who has a child with her, it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلنَّاسَ سُكَارَىٰ وَمَا هُم بِسُكَارَىٰ﴾: the people and the readers agreed on (سُكَارَى ومَاهُمْ بِسُكَارى). Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to me from Mughīra from Ibrāhīm from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he read (وَتَرى الناسَ سَكْرَى وَمَا هُمْ بِسَكْرَى), and that is a good option in Arabic (because it is on a par with al-halkā and al-jarḥā ("the perishing", "the wounded"), and not in the manner of al-nashwān and al-nashāwā ("tipsy")). The Arabs take fāʿil, faʿīl and faʿil, when the one so described is like the sick, the felled or the wounded, and pluralize it on the pattern faʿlā; they made faʿlā a mark of the plural of everyone afflicted with chronic illness, harm or perishing, and they do not care whether its singular [Translator's note: the text has «واحه», evidently for «واحده»] is fāʿil, faʿīl or faʿlān. So sakrā, dropping the alif, was chosen because of the terror and fright of that Day. Had it been said (sakrā) on the basis that the plural takes the feminine and so is like a singular feminine, it would have been a valid option, as Allah said: ﴿وللهِ الأسْماءُ الحُسنَى﴾ and ﴿والقُرونَ الأُولَى﴾; and al-nās are a collective, so it is permissible for that to apply to them. The Arabs have said: "qad jāʾatka al-nās" ("the people have come to you", feminine verb). One of them recited to me:
أضحت بنو عامر غَضْبَى أنوفُهم * أَنّى عفوت فلا عارٌ ولا باس
(The Banū ʿĀmir became angry, their noses bristling, because I pardoned; yet there is no shame and no harm.)
He said ghaḍbā for "the noses", in the way I have explained to you.
It is mentioned that one of the readers read (وَتُرَى الناسَ), and that is a good option. He means something like your saying "ruʾīta annaka qāʾim" and "ruʾītuka qāʾiman" ("you were seen to be standing"); you make (سكارى) be in the position of the accusative, because (تُرَى) needs two things which it puts in the accusative, as verbs of thinking (al-ẓann) need.

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ﴾: the hāʾ in (عَلَيه) and in (أَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ) refers to the rebellious devil. Its meaning: it has been decreed for him that he will lead astray whoever follows him.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿مُّخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ﴾: He is saying: complete and miscarried. It is permissible [119 b] [Translator's note: to read] mukhallaqatan wa-ghayra mukhallaqatin as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the ḥāl is put in the accusative with definite and indefinite nouns alike, as you say "hal min rajulin yuḍrabu mujarradan?" ("is there a man who is beaten stripped?"). This is a ḥāl and not a naʿt (adjective).
His saying: ﴿لِّنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِي ٱلأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ﴾: He began (ونُقِرُّ فى الأرحَام) anew and did not refer it back to (لنبيّن). Had (ليُبيِّن) been read, meaning "so that Allah may make clear to you", it would have been correct, but I have not heard it.
His saying: ﴿وَمِنكُمْ مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ﴾: to the lowest stage of life. ﴿لِكَيْلاَ يَعْلَمَ﴾: He is saying: so that he does not understand (anything) after his former understanding.
His saying: (ورَبَت): the readers read (وَرَبَتْ) (from tarbū, "it swells"). Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Tamīmī narrated to me from Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī that he read ﴿¤هْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَأتْ﴾ with hamza. If he took it to be from al-rabīʾa, the one who keeps watch for the people, that is an approach: i.e. it rose until it became like a lookout place for the watchman. If he did not mean (by it) this, then it is one of the mistakes the Arabs sometimes make, saying ḥallaʾtu al-sawīq, labbaʾtu bi-l-ḥajj and rathaʾtu al-mayyit [Translator's note: with a spurious hamza]; it is like al-Ḥasan's reading ﴿وَلأَدْرَأتكم بِهِ﴾ with hamza. It is among what is rejected in recitation.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿ثَانِيَ عِطْفِهِ﴾ is accusative on the sense of: he disputes, turning his side away — averting himself from the Reminder.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعْبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرْفٍ﴾: it was revealed about some Bedouins of the Banū Asad [Translator's note: the text has «أشد»] who moved to Medina with their families, and then made a favour of that to the Prophet ﷺ [Translator's note: the text has «قامتنّوا», evidently for «فامتنّوا»], saying: "A man (after a man) of a tribe embraces Islam, while we have brought you our families." When they were given some of the alms and their livestock and horses remained safe, they said: "What an excellent religion this is!" And if they were not given any of the alms and their livestock did not remain safe, they turned back from Islam. That is His saying ﴿يَعْبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرْفٍ فَإِنْ أَصَابَهُ خَيْرٌ ٱطْمَأَنَّ بِهِ﴾: He is saying: he remains in it; ﴿وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ ٱنْقَلَبَ﴾: and goes back.
His saying: ﴿خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآُخِرَةَ﴾: he has been cheated of both. It is reported of Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj alone that he read (خاسِر الدنيا والآخرة). All is correct, and the meaning is the same.

farraa:12-13.t:
His saying: ﴿يَدْعُو مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ means the idols.
Then He said: ﴿يَدْعُو لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ﴾, and the exegesis has come as: "he calls upon one whose harm is nearer than his benefit"; the lām has intervened between them. Thus it is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (يَدْعو من ضَرُّه). We have not found the Arabs saying "ḍarabtu la-akhāka" or "raʾaytu la-Zaydan afḍala minka". Yet the readers have agreed on it. We consider that it is permissible because (مَن) is a word in which the case-ending does not show; so it was permitted — [Translator's note: manuscript] B: so it was deemed permissible — to interpose the lām before the noun, since the case-ending does not show in it. It is reported of the Arabs that they said "ʿindī la-mā ghayruhu khayrun minhu" ("I have what something other than it is better than"), interposing the lām before what makes [Translator's note: the predicate] nominative, whereas the lām's place should have been in (ḍarruhu), and in your saying "ʿindī mā la-ghayruhu khayrun minhu". This is the explanation of the reading, out of following [Translator's note: the received text]. And it may be that His saying is: ﴿ذَلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلالُ البَعِيدُ يَدْعُو﴾, so that you make (يدعو) part of the ṣila (relative clause) of (الضَّلالُ البَعِيدُ), implying the hāʾ in (يدعو), and then begin the speech anew with the lām, saying (لمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أقربُ مِن نَفْعِهِ لَبِئسَ المَوْلَي), like your saying, in the conditional manner, "la-mā faʿalta la-huwa khayrun laka" ("what you have done is surely better for you"). That is a strong option in Arabic.
And there is another option that has not been read: that you give kasra to the lām in (لمن), meaning "he calls to one [120 a] whose harm is nearer than his benefit", so that the lām is on a par with ilā, as He said ﴿الحَمْدُ لِلّهِ الذِى هَدَانا لِهَذَا﴾, i.e. "to this" (ilā hādhā). You say in speech: "daʿawtu ilā fulān" and "daʿawtu li-fulān" with one meaning. Were it not for the dislike of departing from the transmitted reports and the consensus, it would have been a good option of reading. His saying (يَدْعو) that comes after (البَعِيدُ) would then be a repetition of His saying ﴿يدعو من دون الله﴾ — yadʿū repeated, as you say "he calls, he calls, persistently". This is a support for whoever gives the lām fatḥa [Translator's note: the text has «نضب», evidently for «نصب»] and does not make (يدعو) fall on (مَنْ). Al-ḍalāl al-baʿīd is the long [Translator's note: straying].

farraa:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿مَن كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَن لَّن يَنصُرَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ is a condition whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is in His saying ﴿فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ﴾. The hāʾ in (His saying) ﴿يَنصُرَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ refers to the Prophet ﷺ; i.e. whoever of you thinks that Allah will not help Muḥammad to victory so that he makes the religion of Allah prevail, let him put a rope in the ceiling of his house and then strangle himself with it. That is His saying ﴿ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ﴾ by strangling. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ثم ليقطه) [Translator's note: so in the text; probably «ليقطعه» is meant], i.e. the cord, which is the rope. He is saying: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرْ هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُ﴾ — when he does that — his rage. (مَا يَغِيظُ) is in the position of the accusative.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوۤاْ﴾, then He said ﴿إِنَّ ¤للَّهَ﴾: He placed (إنَّ) in their khabar (predicate) and (إنَّ) at the beginning of the speech, while you do not say in speech "inna akhāka innahu dhāhib". It is permissible here because the meaning is like a condition: i.e. whoever was a believer or followed any of these religions, the judgement between them and their reckoning rest with Allah. The Arabs sometimes say: "inna akhāka inna al-dayna ʿalayhi la-kathīr" ("your brother — the debt upon him is great"), placing (إنَّ) in its khabar when it is made nominative only by a noun connected to a mention of it [Translator's note: i.e. containing a pronoun referring back to it], as the poet said:
إنَّ الخليفة إن الله سَرْبله * سِرْبال مُلْك به ترجَى الخواتيم
(The caliph — Allah has clothed him with the garment of sovereignty, through which good endings are hoped for.)
Whoever says this does not say "innaka innaka qāʾim", nor "inna abāka innahu qāʾim", because [Translator's note: in the permitted case] the two nouns differ, so it is good to set the first aside and make the second as though it were the mubtadaʾ (subject); it is good when they differ and ugly when they are the same.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ﴾: He means the inhabitants of the heavens; ﴿وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ means every creature — of the mountains, of the jinn, and the like; ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ وَكَثِيرٌ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ — of the people of obedience. ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْعَذَابُ﴾ indicates that [Translator's note: the meaning is] "and many refused to prostrate", because punishment does not become due upon anyone except for abandoning prostration and obedience. You put it in the nominative by the mention of it that returns in His saying ﴿حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ﴾, so ﴿حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ﴾ is on a par with "refused". Had you used the accusative — "wa-kathīran ḥaqqa [Translator's note: ʿalayhi] al-ʿadhāb" — it would have been a valid option, on a par with His saying ﴿قَرِيقاً هَدَى وفَرِيقاً حَقَّ عليهم الضلالة﴾: the accusative is used when there is a wāw in the phrase and the mention of it returns with a verb that has fallen upon it. The nominative is also possible in it, because of the returning mention, as Allah said ﴿وَالشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الغاوُونَ﴾ and as He said ﴿وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ﴾.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ﴾: He is saying: whomever Allah makes wretched, he has no one to make him happy. It is also read ﴿فمَا لَه من مُكْرَم﴾, meaning: [Translator's note: no] honouring.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَانِ خَصْمَانِ ٱخْتَصَمُواْ فِي رَبِّهِمْ﴾: two parties, the people of two religions. One of the two disputants is the Muslims, and the other the Jews [Translator's note: and] the Christians.
His saying: ﴿ٱخْتَصَمُواْ فِي رَبِّهِمْ﴾: about the religion of their Lord. The Jews and the Christians said to the Muslims: "Our religion is better than your religion, because we preceded you." The Muslims said: "Rather, our religion is better than your religion, because we believe in our Prophet and the Qurʾān, and we believe in your prophets and your books, while you disbelieve in our Prophet and our Book." So the Muslims prevailed over them in argument, and Allah revealed this verse.
His saying: ﴿ٱخْتَصَمُواْ﴾: He did not say ikhtaṣamā (dual) because they are two groups, not two men; had ikhtaṣamā been said, it would have been correct. Similar to it is ﴿وَإن طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ المؤمنِينَ اقتتَلُوا﴾, taking it to refer to the plural; had iqtatalatā been said, it would have been permissible, taking it to refer to the two parties.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿يُصْهَرُ بِهِ مَا فِي بُطُونِهِمْ﴾: it is melted by it. You say: ṣahartu the fat with fire ("I melted the fat").

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَهُمْ مَّقَامِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ﴾: it is related that they hope (to get out) of the Fire, until, when they attempt it, the keepers strike [Translator's note: the text has «ضرت», evidently for «ضربت»] their heads with the hooked rods, so that their heads are caved in, and boiling water is poured into their brains and melts the fat of their bellies. That is His saying in [Translator's note: Sūrat] Ibrāhīm ﴿ويُسْقَى مِنْ مَاءٍ صَدِيدٍ﴾, from what melts out of their bellies and their skins.
His saying: ﴿يَتَجَرعُهُ ولا يكادُ يُسيغُهُ﴾: he is forced to it.

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَلُؤْلُؤاً﴾: the people of Medina read this one and the one in al-Malāʾika [Translator's note: i.e. Sūrat Fāṭir] ﴿ولُؤْلُؤاً﴾ with alif [Translator's note: i.e. accusative], and al-Aʿmash read both in the genitive. I saw it in the copies (maṣāḥif) of ʿAbd Allāh — the one in al-Ḥajj specifically — as (ولُؤْلأ) ﴿وَلاَ تَهَجَّأْه﴾ [Translator's note: these two words, "and do not spell it out", appear in the text with Qurʾānic brackets; they seem to be an aside rather than a quotation]. That is because in his copies the hamza is written with alif in every case, whether what precedes it has kasra, fatḥa or anything else. The one in al-Malāʾika is written in our copies (ولؤلؤ) without alif, and the one in al-Ḥajj (ولؤلؤا) with alif; so the genitive and the accusative are both permissible in the two of them. The accusative in the one in al-Ḥajj is better grounded — because of the alif — than in the one in al-Malāʾika.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: yafʿalūna (imperfect) has been referred back to faʿalū (past) because their meaning is as though one, in alladhī and in what is not alladhī. Had it been said "inna alladhīna kafarū wa-ṣaddū", there would have been nothing in it to ask about. You refer yafʿalūna to faʿalū because you mean: "those who have disbelieved hinder by their disbelief." Your insertion of the wāw is like His saying ﴿وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَلِيَقْترِفُوا﴾: you implied a verb in the wāw along with the hindering, just as you implied it there. Or, if you wish, you say: the hindering on their part is as it were continuous, so yafʿalūna was chosen for them, as though you said: "Those who have disbelieved, and whose habit is hindering." Similar to it is ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرونَ بآياتِ اللهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النبيّينَ﴾, and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ﴿وَقَاتَلُوا الذينَ يأمرونَ بالقِسْطِ﴾. And He said ﴿الذِينَ آمَنُوا وتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾, like that. Similar to it in al-Aḥzāb, in the reading [Translator's note: the text has «قرءاة»] of ʿAbd Allāh: (الذِينَ بَلَّغُوا رِسالات الله وَيَخْشَوْنَه). So there is no harm in referring faʿala back to yafʿalu, as He said ﴿وَقَاتلُوا الذِينَ يأمرونَ﴾, or yafʿalu back to faʿala, as He said ﴿إِنَّ الذينَ كفروا وَيَصُدّون عن سبيل الله﴾.
His saying: ﴿سَوَآءً ٱلْعَاكِفُ فِيهِ وَٱلْبَادِ﴾: al-ʿākif is whoever is of the people of Mecca, and al-bādī is whoever comes to it for ḥajj or ʿumra. The readers agreed on putting (سواء) in the nominative here [Translator's note: the Qurʾānic text printed in this entry is vowelled «سَوَآءً», accusative]. As for His saying [121 a] in al-Sharīʿa [Translator's note: i.e. Sūrat al-Jāthiya]: ﴿سواء مَحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ﴾, al-Aʿmash alone read it in the accusative, and the rest of the readers in the nominative. Whoever uses the accusative makes ﴿جَعَلناه﴾ fall on it; whoever uses the nominative makes the verb fall on the hāʾ and the lām in "for the people", then begins anew and says: ﴿سَوَاءٌ العاكِفُ فِيهِ والبادِ﴾. It is the way of the Arabs to begin anew with sawāʾ when it comes after a word with which the speech is complete; they say: "I passed by a man — alike (sawāʾun) to him are good and evil." The genitive is permissible. They chose the nominative only because (سواء) has the sense of "one", as though you said: "I passed by a man — one (wāḥidun) to him are good and evil." Whoever uses the genitive means "balanced (muʿtadilin) to him are good and evil". They do not say "I passed by a man, muʿtadilun to him are good and evil" (in the nominative), because (muʿtadil) is an explicit verbal form, whereas sawāʾ has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Their treating it as a verbal form is like their treating "I passed by a man, ḥasbika min rajulin" ("sufficient for you as a man") as a verbal form.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ﴾: the bāʾ entered (ilḥād) because its interpretation is: "whoever intends to deviate in it wrongfully." The entry of the bāʾ with (أن) is easier than with al-ilḥād and the like, because prepositions are often implied with (أن), and it is like a condition, so it tolerates the entry of the preposition and its absence, since the case-ending does not show in it; whereas it is rare with maṣdars, because the nominative and genitive show in them. Abū al-Jarrāḥ recited to me:
فلمَّا رَجَتْ بالشّرب هَزّ لها العصا * شَحِيح له عند الإزاء نَهِيم
(When she hoped for a drink, a stingy man with a growl at the trough's spout shook the stick at her.)
(Al-Farrāʾ said: nahīm is a kind of sound.) And Imruʾ al-Qays said:
ألا هل أتاها والحوادث جَمَّة * بأن امرأ القيس بنَ تَمْلِك بَيْقرا
(Has it reached her — and events are many — that Imruʾ al-Qays son of Tamlik has gone to the towns and settled?)
He put the bāʾ on (أنّ) while it is in the position of the nominative, just as He put it on (ilḥādin bi-ẓulmin) while it is in the position of the accusative. They have also put it — meaning the bāʾ — on (مَا) when they intend it as a maṣdar. Qays ibn Zuhayr said:
ألم يأتيك والأنباءُ تنمِى * بما لاقت لبونُ بنى زيادِ
(Has it not reached you — and news spreads — what the milch-camels of the Banū Ziyād met with?)
It is rarer with (ما) than with (أن), because (أن) resembles nouns less than (مَا) does. I heard a Bedouin of Rabīʿa — I had asked him about something — say: "arjū bi-dhāka" ("I hope for that"), meaning "arjū dhāka". Some of the readers read (وَمَن تَرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ), from al-wurūd ("arriving"), as though meaning: "whoever arrives at it or makes his way to it". I do not like it, because waradtu requires a [Translator's note: direct] noun; do you not see that you say "waradnā Makka" and do not say "waradnā fī Makka"? It is permissible if you mean "alighting". It may also be permissible in the dialect of the Ṭayyiʾ, because they say "raghibtu fīka", meaning "raghibtu bika". One of them recited to me about a daughter of his:
وأرغبُ فيهَا عن لَقِيطٍ ورَهْطه * ولكننى عن سِنْبِسٍ لست أرغب
(I hold her too dear for Laqīṭ and his clan, but I do not hold her too dear for Sinbis.)
(He means his daughter.)

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لإِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾: He did not say "bawwaʾnā Ibrāhīma", though it is on a par with His saying ﴿وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنَا بَنِى إسْرائِيلَ مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ﴾. If you wish, you treat ﴿بَوَّأنا﴾ as on a par with jaʿalnā ("We made"); that is how I heard it in the exegesis [Translator's note: the text has «الفسير», evidently for «التفسير»].
And if you wish, it is on a par with His saying ﴿قُلْ عَسَى أنْ يَكُونَ رَدِف لكم بعضُ﴾, whose meaning is "radifakum" ("has come close behind you"). All is correct.

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالاً وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ﴾: ﴿يأتينَ﴾ is the act of the she-camels. It has also [121 b] been read (يأتون), taking it to refer to the riders. Had He said "wa-ʿalā kulli ḍāmirin taʾtī", you would make it a singular verb, because (kull) is added to a singular. It is rare in the speech of the Arabs to say "I passed by every man, standing (qāʾimīna, plural)", yet it is correct. Stronger than it in permissibility is His saying ﴿فَمَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَاجِزِينَ﴾. The plural is permissible with aḥad and with kullu rajul only because their interpretation in the intention may be singular or plural. But when (aḥad) and kull separate [Translator's note: an individual] out of two, nothing but a singular verb for them is permissible. Of that is your saying "kullu rajulin minkumā qāʾimun" ("each man of you two is standing"); it is a mistake to say qāʾimūna or qāʾimāni, because the meaning has brought it back to the singular. Likewise "mā minkumā aḥadun qāʾimūna" or "qāʾimāni" is a mistake for that reason.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُواْ تَفَثَهُمْ﴾ (the lām is quiescent), ﴿وَلْيُوفُواْ نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُواْ﴾: the lāms are quiescent. The people of Medina, ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash made them quiescent, while Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and al-Ḥasan gave them kasra, both after the wāw and elsewhere. Their making it quiescent is a lightening, as you say "wa-hwa qāla dhālika" and "wa-hya qālat dhāka", making the hāʾ quiescent when it is joined to the wāw. Likewise any lām of command joined to a wāw or a fāʾ: most of the speech of the Arabs makes it quiescent. Some of them gave kasra in ﴿ثُمَّ لِيَقْضُواْ﴾, because stopping on (ثُمَّ) is good, whereas it is not good on the fāʾ or the wāw. That is a valid option, except that most of the recitation makes the lām after thumma quiescent.
As for al-tafath, it is the slaughtering of the sacrificial camels and of other animals — cattle and sheep — the shaving of the head, the clipping of the nails, and the like.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ ٱلأَنْعَامُ إِلاَّ مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ in Sūrat al-Māʾida: the strangled, the one beaten to death, the one killed by a fall, the one gored, to the end of the verse.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿فَتَخْطَفُهُ ٱلطَّيْرُ﴾ is among the cases where yafʿalu has been referred back to faʿala. Had you put it in the accusative and said "fa-takhṭafahu al-ṭayru", it would have been a valid option. The Arabs sometimes give a response [Translator's note: with the fāʾ and the accusative] to kaʾannamā, because it has the sense of "it seems to me" and "I think", so it is as though it were referred back to the interpretation of (أنّ); do you not see that you say "it seems to me that you are going, so I will go (fa-adhhaba) with you"? Or, if you wish, you give (كأنَّما) the interpretation of a negation, as though you said: "As if you were an Arab, so that you would be honoured (fa-tukrama)", the interpretation being: "You are not an Arab, so that you would be honoured."

farraa:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِنَّهَا مِن تَقْوَى ٱلْقُلُوبِ﴾: He means "for the deed (al-faʿla)", as He said ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَحَيمٌ﴾, where "min baʿdihi" would also be permissible. Had it been said "fa-innahu min taqwā al-qulūb", it would have been permissible.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾ means the sacrificial camels. He is saying: you may benefit from their milk and from riding them until they are designated or marked [Translator's note: as offerings]; that is the appointed term.
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ مَحِلُّهَآ إِلَىٰ ٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْعَتِيقِ﴾: whatever is an offering for the ʿumra or for a vow is slaughtered when it reaches the House, and whatever is for the ḥajj is slaughtered at Minā. That was placed at Minā so that Mecca would be kept clean.
His saying: ﴿ٱلْعَتِيقِ﴾: it was freed from the tyrants. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-ʿatīq: it was freed from the tyrants. And it is said: from the drowning in the time of Noah.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْمُقِيمِي ٱلصَّلاَةِ﴾: you put (الصلاة) in the genitive when you dropped the nūn. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (والمقيمين الصلاةَ). Had you put (الصلاة) in the accusative while dropping the nūn, it would have been correct. One of them recited to me:
أسَيِّدُ ذو خُرَيِّطَةٍ نهاراً * من المتلقِّطى قَرَدَ القُمَامِ
(A little chief with a little bag by day, one of those who pick up the tangled scraps of the rubbish heaps.)
(and qaradi, genitive). The accusative with the nūn dropped is [122 a] permissible only because the Arabs say nothing but the accusative in the singular; they say "huwa al-ākhidhu ḥaqqahu" ("he is the one who takes his right"), putting al-ḥaqq in the accusative — they say nothing else — while the nūn is absent; so they built the dual and the plural on the singular and used the accusative with the nūn dropped. The proper way in the dual and the plural is the genitive, because their nūn may appear if you wish and be dropped if you wish, whereas in the singular it does not appear; therefore they used the accusative [Translator's note: there]. Had the genitive been used in the singular, that would have been permissible, but I have heard it only in their saying "huwa al-ḍāribu al-rajuli", for they put al-rajul in the genitive and in the accusative; whoever uses the genitive likens it to the manner of their saying "marartu bi-l-ḥasani al-wajhi" ("I passed by the one handsome of face"). When they put it in construct with a pronoun, they say "anta al-ḍāribuhu", "antumā al-ḍāribāhu" and "antum al-ḍāribūhu". The judgement on the hāʾ is that it is genitive in the singular, the dual and the plural; had you intended the accusative by it, it would have been a valid option, because the case-ending does not show in a pronoun. They took the opportunity of the construct because it connects with the genitive more closely than with the accusative, and so they took the stronger of the two ways in respect of connection. Whoever used the accusative ought to say "huwa al-ḍāribu iyyāhu", but I have not heard that.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿صَوَآفَّ﴾: hobbled. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (صَوافِنَ), meaning the standing ones. Al-Ḥasan read (صوافِىَ), saying: purely for Allah.
His saying: ﴿ٱلْقَانِعَ وَٱلْمُعْتَرَّ﴾: al-qāniʿ is the one who asks you (and accepts whatever you give him). Al-muʿtarr is one who is silent and puts himself in your way at the time of slaughter, but does not ask you.

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا﴾: they agreed on the yāʾ; had (تنال) been said, it would have been correct. The meaning of that is that the people of the Jāhiliyya, when they slaughtered them, would sprinkle the blood around the House. When the Muslims made the ḥajj, they wanted to do the same, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلاَ دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَـٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ﴾: sincerity towards Him.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «الناس» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the clause «اتقوا» is the response to the vocative, resumptive, and so is the clause «إن زلزلة ...».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تذهل»; the preposition and its genitive noun «عمَّا» is attached to «تذهل»; «سُكارى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الناس». The wāw in «وما هم» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is a ḥāl of «الناس»; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which operates like laysa. The clause «ولكن عذاب الله شديد» is conjoined to an implied (muqaddar) resumptive clause, i.e.: all this is light, but the punishment of Allah is severe.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «ومن الناس من يجادل» is resumptive; «مَن» is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later; the preposition and its genitive noun «بغير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يجادل»; «مريد» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «شيطان».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (كتب عليه أنه من تولاه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The interpreted maṣdar is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The hāʾ in «أنه» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the conditional clause is the khabar (predicate) of «أنه»; «من» is conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «تولاه» is a khabar. The clause «يضلُّه» is the khabar of the second «أنه», and the second interpreted maṣdar is a mubtadaʾ, i.e.: فإضلاله واقع (then his misguiding is certain); the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause «فإضلاله واقع» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: (إن كنتم في ريب من البعث) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is the response to the vocative, resumptive. The genitive maṣdar «لنبيِّن لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلقناكم»; the clause «ونُقِرّ» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «إلى أجل» is attached to «نقرّ»; His saying «مسمى» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أجل». «طفلا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «نخرجكم», and it is singular because it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الرضا and العدل. The interpreted maṣdar «لتبلغوا» is genitive, attached to an omitted verb conjoined to the clause «نخرجكم», i.e.: ثم نعمِّركم لتبلغوا (then We give you life so that you reach). «لكيلا»: the lām is a preposition and «كي» puts the verb in the accusative; the interpreted maṣdar «لكيلا يعلم» is genitive, attached to «يرد», and «شيئا» is the object of «عِلْم». The clause «وترى» is conjoined to the clause «إنا خلقناكم», and the conditional clause is conjoined to the clause «وترى الأرض». His saying «هامدة»: a ḥāl of «الأرض».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «ذلك بأن الله هو الحق» is resumptive. The interpreted maṣdar is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «ذلك»; «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position; and the second interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to the first.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The interpreted maṣdar «وأن الساعة ...» is conjoined to the preceding maṣdar, and the clause «لا ريب فيها» is a second khabar (predicate) of «أنَّ». The preposition and its genitive noun «في القبور» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «ومن الناس من يجادل» is conjoined to «من الناس من يجادل» in verse (3). The preposition and its genitive noun «بغير علم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يجادل».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «ثاني» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of {يُجَادِلُ}; the maṣdar «ليضل» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يُجَادِلُ}; the clause «له في الدنيا خزي» is a ḥāl of the agent of {يُجَادِلُ}; the preposition and its genitive noun «في الدنيا» is attached to a ḥāl of «خزي»; and the clause «نذيقه» is conjoined to the clause «له في الدنيا خزي».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «بما»: the bāʾ is a preposition, and «ما» is a relative noun, genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The clause «ذلك بما قدَّمت» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) of an implied (muqaddar) verb of saying, i.e.: قائلين له (saying to him), and this saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «نذيقه». The maṣdar «وأن الله ليس بظلام» is conjoined to «ما». The faʿʿāl pattern here is for attribution (nasab), i.e.: not one possessing injustice. The lām in «للعبيد» is redundant (zāʾida) for strengthening (taqwiya), and «العبيد» is the object of «ظلام».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «ومن الناس من يعبد» is conjoined to the clause {وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجَادِلُ} in verse (8). The preposition and its genitive noun «على حرف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يعبد». The clause «فإن أصابه خير» is conjoined to the clause «ومن الناس من يعبد»; the preposition and its genitive noun «على وجهه» is attached to a ḥāl of the agent of «انقلب»; the clause «خسر الدنيا» is a ḥāl of the agent of «انقلب». The clause «ذلك هو الخسران» is resumptive: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) is «الخسران», and «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «يدعو» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; the clause «ذلك هو الضلال» is resumptive, and «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «يدعو» is resumptive. «لمَن ضرّه»: the lām is redundant (zāʾida) in the object, for emphasis (taʾkīd), and «مَن» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e.: يدعو مَنْ ضرُّه أقرب (he calls one whose harm is nearer); «ضرّه أقرب» are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أقرب». This view is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd]: «يدعو مَن ضرُّه أقرب». The clause «ضرُّه أقرب» is the ṣila (relative clause). The lām in «لبئس» occurs in the response to an oath, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the one specified (al-makhṣūṣ) is omitted, its implied form being: هو.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «جنات» is the second object, and the clause «تجري» is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «مَن» is conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «كان» is the khabar (predicate). «أنْ» is lightened from the heavy one (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the maṣdar «أَنْ لن ينصره» stands in place of the two objects of ẓanna. The clause «يظن» is the khabar of kāna, and the clause «لن ينصره» is the khabar of the lightened «أن». The clause «فليمدد» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the lām is for command, and the verb with it is jussive (majzūm). The clause «هل يُذْهبن» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; «ما» is a relative noun, the object of «يُذْهبن».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «وكذلك»: the wāw is resumptive, and the kāf is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: أنزلناه إنزالا مثل ذلك الإنزال (We sent it down a sending down like that sending down). The clause «أنزلناه» is resumptive; «آيات» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ; and the maṣdar «وأن الله يهدي» is conjoined to the hāʾ in «أنزلناه».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «إن الله يفصل» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن الذين»; the two adverbs «بينهم» and «يوم» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يفصل».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: (ألم تر أن الله يسجد له) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of «تر», and the preposition and its genitive noun «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); the preposition and its genitive noun «من الناس» is attached to an adjective (ṣifa) of «كثير». His saying «وكثير»: conjoined to the preceding «كثير», and the clause «حقَّ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كثير». The clause «ومن يهن» is resumptive; «مَن» is a conditional noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «فما له من مكرم» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «مِن» is redundant (zāʾida); «مُكْرِم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition and its genitive noun «له» is attached to the khabar (predicate). The clause «إن الله يفعل» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: «هذان خصمان»: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause «اختصموا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «خصمان». The clause «فالذين كفروا ...» is conjoined to the resumptive one, «هذان خصمان», and the clause «قطِّعَت» is the khabar of the relative noun. The preposition and its genitive noun «من نار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of «ثياب»; the clause «يُصَبُّ مِنْ فَوْقِ رُءُوسِهِمُ الْحَمِيم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «لهم».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «يُصهر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of {الْحَمِيمُ}; the preposition and its genitive noun «في بطونهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); His saying «والجلود»: a noun conjoined to «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «ولهم مقامع» is conjoined to the clause {يُصَبُّ}; the preposition and its genitive noun «من حديد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «مقامع».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «كل» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعيدوا», and «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); the implied form is: they are returned into it at every time of wanting. The clause «أعيدوا» is resumptive, and the maṣdar «أن يخرجوا» is the object of «أرادوا». «من غم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, a badal (substitute) of «منها», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), with the pronoun implied (muqaddar), the implied form being: «من غمها» (from its anguish). The clause «ذوقوا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) of an implied verb of saying, i.e.: the angels say to them, and the implied saying is conjoined to the clause «أعيدوا».
